Product surfaces that hand an agent a ticket and return a pull request, such as an issue tracker, a review tool or an IDE side panel.
Demos and onboarding that explain how an agent works step by step, with a real approval gate.
whenNotToUse: Use research-run for a research agent that reads sources and writes a cited report.
Use agent-approvals for an inbox of pending approvals across many agents and tools.
Use agent-orchestrator when several agents work in parallel on parts of one job.
Use code-review for reviewing a finished pull request line by line with comments.

name: agent-tasks
title: Agent tasks
description: A home for background coding agents: start a task on a repository and branch, watch each card move from queued to running to ready for review, and open a pull request from the result.
whenToUse: A product surface where people hand coding tasks to background agents and come back later to review, open a pull request, retry or archive.
Dashboards for automated maintenance runs, such as dependency upgrades, flaky test fixes or codemods, where each run ends in a branch with a diff and checks.
Any queue of long running agent jobs where the current step, the elapsed time and a clear finished state matter more than a transcript.
whenNotToUse: Use agent-run to follow one live agent run in detail, with its plan, tool calls and output.
Use code-review when people need to read the diff line by line and leave comments; this block only summarizes the change.
Use agent-approvals when the agent pauses for a person to approve a risky action before it continues.
Use agent-routines for scheduled, recurring agent jobs rather than one-off tasks.
Use ai-composer for a chat style prompt box without a task list.

name: ai-answer
title: AI answer
description: One AI answer set like a clean article: it thinks, shows its sources as small cards with colored marks, and streams a formatted answer where every citation lights the sentence it supports. Copy, regenerate with options, rate, share, page through versions and ask a related question in place.
whenToUse: An answer page where one question gets one well formatted, cited answer that people read, copy and share.
Docs and help center assistants that must show where each claim comes from.
Internal knowledge search where the answer mixes prose, steps, a comparison table and code.
whenNotToUse: Use ai-chat for a back and forth conversation with many turns kept on screen.
Use research-run for long multi step research that plans searches and reads many sources before writing.
Use ai-side-panel when the assistant sits next to a document or app the person is working in.
Use ai-inline-edit to rewrite a selection in place rather than answer a question.

name: ai-chat
title: AI chat
description: A full-screen AI chat where answers stream in as markdown with folding reasoning, tool chips and cited sources. People can switch chats and models, edit or retry a message into versions, rate replies and stop a reply mid-stream.
whenToUse: A multi turn assistant inside a product page, drawer or dashboard card, with streaming answers, reasoning, tools and citations.
Any place users need to retry, edit, rate or copy answers and switch models mid conversation.
Prototyping an LLM feature: with no props it plays a realistic scripted conversation and answers new messages with simulated replies.
whenNotToUse: Use ai-composer when you only need the prompt box with attachments, mentions and commands.
Use ai-answer for a single question and a long, article like answer with sources.
Use agent-run or research-run when the work is a multi step agent run with a plan and progress rather than a conversation.
Use model-picker for a standalone model selector with pricing and context details.

name: ai-composer
title: AI composer
description: The prompt box at the bottom of an AI app: files upload in place, / opens commands, @ inserts mentions, a model and effort menu sits in the toolbar, and the send button turns into a stop control ringed by the reply's progress.
whenToUse: The prompt box of an assistant, a coding agent or an in-product AI feature where people attach files, mention docs and pick a model.
A new chat screen that should open on a greeting and suggestions, then show the first exchange.
Any place that needs a streaming send and stop control with honest progress and keyboard first commands.
whenNotToUse: Use ai-chat for a full conversation with history, message actions and a sidebar of chats.
Use ai-inline-edit to rewrite a selection inside a document instead of chatting about it.
Use voice-agent when speech is the main input and the reply is spoken.
Use model-picker when the job is comparing and choosing models rather than sending a prompt.

name: ai-feature-launch
title: AI feature launch
description: An in-product launch card for an AI feature. A looping mini demo plays above a three-step tour (inline rewrite, thread summary, ask your workspace), with benefit rows, an admin-gated "Enable for my workspace" switch, and Try it now and Learn more actions.
whenToUse: Announcing a new AI feature inside the product, with a tour of what it does and a switch to turn it on for the workspace.
Admin-gated rollouts where an admin enables AI for everyone and members can still try it.
A what's new modal or popover that needs to look polished in a launch clip.
whenNotToUse: Multi-step configuration with real inputs (models, data sources): use ai-setup-wizard.
Ongoing activation tasks: use onboarding-checklist.
A long changelog or release notes page: render the entries as a page instead.

name: ai-inline-edit
title: AI inline edit
description: A document you edit with AI in place: \u2318K on a selection, watch the rewrite stream in as a diff, accept each change, and Tab through ghost text.
whenToUse: Rewriting a selection: shorten, clarify, change tone or fix grammar in place.
Inline autocomplete while writing documents or messages.
Any AI suggestion that should be reviewed as a diff before it lands.
whenNotToUse: Rich formatting such as headings, lists or links; the block edits plain paragraphs.
Asking questions about a page; use ai-side-panel.
A single prompt box without a document; use ai-composer.

name: ai-insight-card
title: AI insight card
description: A KPI card that explains itself. Explain streams a short reason for the change and ranks three drivers with contribution bars. A numbered annotation lights up on the sparkline as each driver is read, and follow-up chips ask the next question in place.
whenToUse: A dashboard KPI where readers ask why it moved, such as net revenue, MRR, signups or churn.
Weekly business reviews and finance dashboards that want an explanation next to the number.
Products adding AI analysis to existing analytics without a separate chat.
whenNotToUse: Open ended questions across many tables: use ask-your-data.
A plain number with no explanation: use metric-card or stat-card.
Dense multi series charts: use a full chart component.

name: ai-search-bar
title: AI search bar
description: A search card for an app or docs, where typing lists grouped results right away (Docs, Customers, Issues) and pressing Tab streams a short AI answer on top. The answer's numbered citations point to the results below it.
whenToUse: A product or docs search where people mix finding a page or record with asking a question.
Support and success tools that search docs, customers and tickets in one place.
A command bar or search dialog that should offer an AI answer without leaving the results.
whenNotToUse: Use ai-answer for a full answer page with long formatted answers, follow ups and feedback.
Use ai-chat for a back and forth conversation.
Use ai-command for an action palette that runs commands rather than searches content.

name: ai-setup-wizard
title: AI setup wizard
description: A three-step setup card for turning on an AI feature. You connect Notion, Google Drive, Confluence or Zendesk and watch each one sync. Then you pick the model, tone and guardrails, and ask a test question whose answer streams with numbered citations before you go live.
whenToUse: Turning on an AI answers feature for a support, sales or internal knowledge team, like Intercom Fin, Zendesk AI or Notion Q&A.
Onboarding admins to a copilot that needs data sources, a model choice and guardrails before it is enabled.
A landing page or product tour section that shows the full setup in one short, looping clip.
whenNotToUse: Configuring an agent's instructions, tools and files in depth: use agent-builder.
Only choosing a model: use model-picker.
A full conversation after setup: use ai-chat. The test step answers one question at a time.
Monitoring a running agent: use agent-status.

name: ai-side-panel
title: AI side panel
description: An assistant docked beside a page that reads it and edits it: ask about the page or a selected passage, review each edit as a word diff, and apply it with a tint sweep on the page and one-click undo.
whenToUse: An assistant next to a document or record that can summarize it and propose edits.
Copilot style help where edits must be approved, applied visibly and undone.
Asking about a selected passage or table without leaving the page.
whenNotToUse: A standalone conversation; use ai-chat.
Rewriting a passage in place with no side panel; use ai-inline-edit.
A single prompt box; use ai-composer.
Showing an autonomous agent's steps; use agent-run.

name: api-keys
title: API keys
description: API key management where Create key unfolds into its form and each secret is shown once.
whenToUse: The developer settings page of an API product.
Key management with scopes, environments, and a one-time secret reveal.
Revoking keys where a stray click must not fire.
whenNotToUse: Use webhooks for event endpoints and signing secrets.
Use integrations for OAuth connections to other apps.
Use roles-permissions for user access.

name: availability-picker
title: Availability picker
description: Find a meeting time across people and see the choice come together.
whenToUse: Picking a meeting time that works for several attendees.
Booking flows that show a few days and open slots with a confirmation step.
whenNotToUse: Use calendar or date-picker to pick a single date.
Use time-picker for a free time input.
Use event-invite to show and respond to an invite.

name: billing-overview
title: Billing overview
description: A billing page where the plan card morphs into a picker and usage, invoices, and card follow.
whenToUse: The billing settings page of a SaaS app.
Pages that show plan, usage, payment method, and invoices together.
Plan changes that should happen in place without leaving billing.
whenNotToUse: Use plan-comparison or usage-pricing on a public pricing page.
Use cancel-flow for the cancellation journey.
Use usage-meter to show a single quota elsewhere.

name: budget-variance
title: Budget variance
description: Budget against actual operating spend by department as aligned bullet charts, with favorable and unfavorable variance, a month, quarter and year to date switch that springs every bar, in-place drill-down into budget lines, and a total row.
whenToUse: Monthly close and budget review screens that compare planned and actual operating spend by department or cost center.
Finance dashboards where a controller needs to see at a glance which teams are over, which are under, and by how much.
Any plan against actual comparison with a meaningful tolerance band, such as headcount cost or cloud spend by team.
whenNotToUse: Use mrr-waterfall to explain how a single total moved from one value to another.
Use usage-forecast to project spend against a cap over time.
Use a line or bar chart to show a trend across many periods; this block compares one window at a time.
Use a sortable data table when there are dozens of cost centers and sorting matters more than the visual comparison.

name: call-insights
title: Call insights
description: A sales call insights card where talk time, flagged pricing, competitor and objection moments, an AI summary and owned next steps sit in one view. Selecting a moment plays its quote, and checking off next steps lowers the deal risk.
whenToUse: A deal page that shows the latest sales call with talk ratio, flagged moments, summary and next steps.
A call review queue for sales managers who coach on talk time and objection handling.
A research or support tool that recaps a recorded customer call with jump-to-quote clips.
whenNotToUse: Full transcript reading or editing: use transcript-studio.
An internal meeting recap without a prospect or deal: use meeting-summary.
A pipeline overview across many deals: use a table such as crm-contacts.

name: cancel-flow
title: Cancel flow
description: A cancellation flow that answers each reason with a tailored offer and a calm hold-to-cancel.
whenToUse: Subscription cancellation in billing settings with a reason step and a retention offer.
Flows that offer a discount, pause, or downgrade before confirming the cancel.
whenNotToUse: Use dialog with hold-to-confirm for a one step destructive action without offers.
Use plan-comparison when people are choosing a plan rather than leaving.
Use billing-overview for the billing page itself.

name: cart-drawer
title: Cart drawer
description: Products fly into the cart, counts roll, and a drawer handles quantities, shipping progress, and checkout.
whenToUse: Product listings where people add several items and review them in a side cart.
Stores that show a free shipping threshold and promo codes before checkout.
Demos of an add to cart interaction with clear feedback on where the item went.
whenNotToUse: Use checkout-flow for a full multi-step checkout with address and payment.
Use checkout-summary when you only need the order summary and totals.
Use drawer for a generic side panel that is not a cart.

name: catch-up
title: Catch up
description: A catch me up digest for when you return, where one button reads Slack, Linear, GitHub and Gmail for the range you pick and streams back a short ranked summary: Needs you, Decisions made, Shipped and FYI. Each item is one sentence with its source mark, people and a jump link, and marking items as read clears them with a smooth collapse.
whenToUse: A home or inbox screen that summarizes what happened across connected tools while the user was away.
An AI assistant feature that turns hundreds of notifications into a short ranked list with jump links.
A weekly or daily digest preview inside a product's notification settings.
whenNotToUse: A live notification feed where every event matters; use a plain activity list instead.
A long-form report or meeting summary with paragraphs; use a document view or ai-chat.
Approving agent actions; use agent-approvals.

name: checkout-live
title: Live checkout
description: A subscription checkout whose summary recomputes as you edit, then glides to the centre and unfolds into a receipt.
whenToUse: Upgrade from a free plan to a paid team plan.
Paid signup where seats and add-ons change the price.
A self serve checkout that needs coupons and tax by country.
whenNotToUse: A physical goods cart with shipping; use checkout-flow.
Only showing totals without payment; use checkout-summary.
Comparing plans before choosing; use plan-comparison.

name: checkout-summary
title: Checkout summary
description: An order summary with a promo code that becomes a chip, discount and tax lines, and pay button states.
whenToUse: The last step before a hosted checkout such as a Stripe session redirect.
A single product purchase with launch discounts or promo codes.
A pricing page side panel that confirms the final total.
whenNotToUse: Use checkout-flow when you collect shipping and card details in the page.
Use cart-drawer for a cart with several items and quantities.
Use billing-overview for an existing subscription's invoices and plan.

name: choropleth-explorer
title: Choropleth explorer
description: A filled-region map that shades every state or region by revenue, growth or penetration on a stepped scale, with a country switch (United States, Canada, Brazil, United Kingdom, France, Germany, Italy, Australia), a hoverable legend, a synced ranked list and a camera zoom into local detail.
whenToUse: Sales, revenue or usage dashboards that break a metric down by state, country or territory.
Market coverage and penetration reviews where a region's own subareas explain its number.
Any analytics view where readers compare neighbouring areas and need the ranked numbers beside the map.
whenNotToUse: Use offices-map to place pins at specific locations such as offices or stores.
Use revenue-globe for flows and totals on a spinning globe when geography is ambience rather than the comparison.
Use a bar chart or sortable table when the regions are few, or when area size would mislead (a large, sparse region draws more attention than a small, dense one).

name: cohort-retention
title: Cohort retention
description: A cohort retention triangle that morphs into retention curves and rewashes by segment.
whenToUse: Growth or customer success dashboards comparing how signup cohorts retain month over month.
Views that need both the cohort triangle and retention curves from the same data.
whenNotToUse: Use journey-flow for paths between funnel steps.
Use activity-heatmap for activity by day rather than by cohort.
Use revenue-explorer for revenue over time.

name: connected-scatter
title: Connected scatter
description: A connected scatterplot of monthly CAC against LTV where the path draws itself in, a scrubber moves a head along the curve, and a channel switch morphs the path against a shaded 3x target line.
whenToUse: A growth or finance screen that shows whether unit economics are moving toward or away from a target ratio.
Comparing how a few segments or channels travelled through the same two metrics over the same months.
A report where specific months (a pricing change, a campaign) explain a turn and deserve a label on the path.
whenNotToUse: Use line-chart or metric-explorer when time itself is the axis and one metric is enough.
Use efficient-frontier for risk against return of a portfolio you can change.
Use a plain scatter or beeswarm when points have no time order to connect.

name: credit-topup
title: Credit top-up
description: A card for buying AI credits. It shows the balance with a 14 day usage chart and how many days are left, three preset packs with bonus badges, a custom amount slider with a live price, auto top-up with a threshold and the saved Visa or Mastercard. When you buy, the new balance rolls in like an odometer.
whenToUse: Selling prepaid AI credits or tokens with volume bonuses.
A billing settings section where people also manage auto top-up and their card.
An out of credits moment where the balance, burn rate and a one click refill belong together.
whenNotToUse: Subscription plan changes with seats and billing cycles: use a plan picker or checkout-live.
Collecting a new card number: use a card form or a hosted payment element, then pass the saved card here.
Read-only usage reporting: use a usage meter or a chart.

name: customer-galaxy
title: Customer galaxy
description: 2,400 accounts as a drifting galaxy that spirals into clusters by plan, region or health.
whenToUse: Customer success or revenue pages to explore where MRR and risk concentrate.
Showcase views that cluster thousands of accounts by plan, region, or health.
whenNotToUse: Use customers-table when people need to find and act on specific accounts.
Use semantic-zoom for hierarchical data like teams and projects.
Use bar-chart for simple totals by segment.

name: delivery-tracker
title: Delivery tracker
description: A live order tracker whose marker glides between stops while the arrival time rolls.
whenToUse: Order status pages that follow a delivery from dispatch to door.
Tracking screens with a live arrival time and an event history.
Deliveries where people can message or call the courier.
whenNotToUse: Use timeline for a static list of past events.
Use progress when a single percentage is enough.
Use support-conversation for a full chat with support.

name: document-extract
title: Document extraction
description: Turns a document into typed data with a model and shows where every value came from: fields fill in as the page is read, and hovering a value lights its source on the PDF.
whenToUse: Accounts payable, logistics or back office tools that turn invoices, receipts, emails or forms into records a person accepts before saving.
Any extraction flow where a reviewer needs to see exactly where each value came from and fix the few the model was unsure about.
Demos and settings pages for a structured output feature, with the schema and live typed JSON one tab away.
whenNotToUse: Use ai-answer for a written answer with citations rather than typed fields.
Use knowledge-base to search and cite across many documents instead of reading one.
Use ai-inline-edit to rewrite text in place rather than pull values out of it.
Use agent-approvals when the decision is approving an agent's actions, not reviewing extracted values.

name: domain-verify
title: Domain verify
description: A custom domain setup card where customers add a domain and copy the DNS records. A live checker then polls resolvers, marks each record valid, not found or misconfigured with a one-line fix, and finishes with the domain verified and the SSL certificate issued.
whenToUse: Letting customers serve an app, docs site, status page or storefront from their own domain.
Verifying a sending domain for email (SPF, DKIM, DMARC) before turning on delivery.
Any setup step where a person must copy values into a third party and wait for propagation.
whenNotToUse: Buying or searching domains: use a search field with results instead.
Managing many domains at once: use a table with one row per domain and open this card per domain.
One-off copy of a single value: a copy-button next to the value is enough.

name: env-variables
title: Environment variables
description: An environment variables and secrets manager with masked values, per-environment scope toggles, .env paste import with duplicate and invalid key warnings, write-only sensitive values, an environment diff by fingerprint, and a redeploy banner.
whenToUse: A settings screen where developers manage configuration and secrets across development, preview, and production.
Onboarding a project by pasting an existing .env file and scoping it to environments in one step.
Auditing drift between environments before a release, such as a key set in Preview but missing in Production.
whenNotToUse: Use api-keys for creating, scoping, and revoking access tokens that your product issues to its users.
Use a plain form for a handful of fixed settings that are not per environment.

name: eval-suite
title: Eval suite
description: Run an evaluation suite on a new version of an LLM feature against its baseline: results stream in case by case, and regressions and fixes are called out with the cases behind them.
whenToUse: Regression testing an LLM feature before shipping a new prompt, model or agent version.
CI style eval dashboards where people need the overall score, the per category picture and the exact cases that broke in one place.
Triage of failing cases with an LLM judge: read both outputs, check the rubric, then accept the change or file an issue.
whenNotToUse: Use prompt-studio to edit a prompt and try it on one test case at a time.
Use model-arena for a blind side by side vote between models on a single prompt.
Use agent-run to follow one agent run step by step rather than scoring a suite.
Use token-inspector to look at token level probabilities of a single reply.

name: exploded-view
title: Exploded view
description: A scroll driven exploded view where a live phone screen built from five CSS 3D layers lies back, separates in depth with labels that follow each layer, takes each layer into focus, and then reassembles.
whenToUse: A showpiece section that shows a product is built with care, by literally taking its screen apart.
Explaining the layers of a design system or UI kit: tokens, grid, content, controls and overlays.
A launch page moment between the hero and the feature list, where one strong scroll interaction earns its place.
whenNotToUse: Use zoom-into-ui to fly into parts of a flat product screen and explain features in place.
Use scroll-story when the story is a sequence of product states rather than the structure of one screen.
Use a static screenshot or feature-illustration where scroll driven motion would compete with nearby sections.

name: feature-bento
title: Feature bento
description: A six cell feature bento where small, real product UI acts each feature out on hover.
whenToUse: A landing page features section that should show the product rather than list it.
Launch pages where each capability has one clear, demonstrable behavior.
whenNotToUse: Long feature lists or comparison tables. Use Plan comparison.
A guided walkthrough with order. Use Scroll story.
Cards that open into detail. Use Spotlight grid.

name: feature-voting
title: Feature voting
description: A public feature request board where votes roll digit by digit and the button fills with the accent. Top, New and Trending reorder the rows with one smooth move. A built-in composer suggests similar requests as you type, so people vote instead of posting duplicates.
whenToUse: A public feature request page where customers vote and suggest ideas.
An in-app Give feedback panel that shows what is planned and shipped.
A customer portal that needs to deflect duplicate requests before they are posted.
whenNotToUse: A full roadmap with columns per stage: use a kanban style board.
One off feedback on a single page or screen: use a short feedback form.
Release notes of what already shipped: use changelog-feed.

name: feedback-board
title: Feedback board
description: A feature request board with a submit form that finds similar requests, upvotes, top and new sorting, status filters, and comments.
whenToUse: A public or in app board where customers suggest and vote on features.
Beta programs that need a lightweight place for requests and team replies.
whenNotToUse: One to one support conversations; use support-conversation or support-widget.

name: gantt-timeline
title: Gantt timeline
description: A project timeline with draggable, resizable bars, dependency arrows that follow them, and animated zoom.
whenToUse: Planning work across weeks or months where tasks depend on each other.
Roadmaps that people reschedule by dragging, with undo and conflict warnings.
Phase based plans where finished phases can be folded into a summary bar.
whenNotToUse: Use project-board for status columns without dates.
Use week-calendar for time slots within days.
Use timeline for a read-only list of dated events.

name: goal-tracker
title: Goal tracker
description: A team goals card where objectives open into key results with owners, confidence and progress bars. A weekly check-in updates a value, confidence and note in place, fills the bar and recalculates the objective, and a quarter selector steps from last quarter's final scores to next quarter's planning.
whenToUse: Showing a team's quarterly objectives and key results with owners and confidence.
Collecting a lightweight weekly check-in (value, confidence, note) without leaving the page.
Comparing the active quarter against last quarter's final scores.
whenNotToUse: A single KPI with a trend line; use a metric or stat card.
Task or project tracking with assignees and due dates; use a task list or kanban block.
Org-wide goal trees with parent and child alignment; this card is one level deep.

name: help-center
title: Help center
description: A help center with instant search, topic cards, and popular articles that open into a readable article with an outline and feedback.
whenToUse: A public help center or knowledge base
In-app help with searchable articles
Support portals that deflect tickets with good answers
whenNotToUse: Developer API reference with a nav tree, use docs-sidebar
A short FAQ on a marketing page, use faq-section
Live chat with support, use support-conversation

name: hero-signup
title: Hero signup
description: A full screen waitlist hero on a soft, drifting mesh gradient: the email field validates as you type and its button grows into the confirmation with your place in line.
whenToUse: Waitlists, early access, and launch pages where the email is the only ask.
Pages that want a calm but alive first impression without product screenshots.
whenNotToUse: Signup that needs a password, SSO choice, or consent up front; use Sign up form.
A newsletter box further down the page; use Newsletter signup.

name: horizon-chart
title: Horizon chart
description: A horizon chart that stacks fourteen daily series as compact folded rows, with a synced crosshair, a sort by name, peak or latest, a band count setting that folds every row on one spring, and a legend that explains how to read the bands.
whenToUse: Operations or growth dashboards comparing many markets, services or products against their own baseline over weeks or months.
Monitoring views where the reader scans for which rows broke from normal and when, then reads exact values on one day.
Any time series comparison where small multiples of line charts would need too much height.
whenNotToUse: Use small-multiples when there are only a few series and the reader needs axes and exact levels in each panel.
Use ridgeline to compare distributions rather than values over time.
Use streamgraph to show how parts add up to a total over time.
Use line-chart for one to four series that should be read precisely against a y axis.

name: inbox-triage
title: Inbox triage
description: Process a focused inbox with archive, snooze, and restore actions.
whenToUse: A queue of messages or requests that need archive, snooze, or restore decisions.
Inboxes where rows expand in place to show details and actions.
whenNotToUse: Use inbox-sidebar for mail navigation with folders and counts.
Use notification-center for system notifications.
Use swipe-actions for touch-first lists with gesture actions.

name: integrations
title: Integrations
description: An integrations directory where Connect morphs to Connected and the filters recount as you go.
whenToUse: Settings or marketplace pages for third party connections.
Directories with search, category filters, and Connect buttons.
Connections that need sync settings and a safe disconnect.
whenNotToUse: Use webhooks for outgoing event endpoints.
Use api-keys for developer credentials.

name: invite-people
title: Invite people
description: Invite teammates with roles, bulk paste validation, a seat meter, and avatars that fly into a pending list.
whenToUse: Inviting several people at once by name or email, with a role for each.
Plans with a seat limit where people should see the effect of an invite before sending.
Flows where users paste a messy list from a spreadsheet and need clear per-entry errors.
whenNotToUse: Use team-members to manage people who already joined.
Use roles-permissions to edit what each role can do.
Use tag-input for a plain chip field without a directory, roles, or seats.

name: invoice-studio
title: Invoice studio
description: An editable invoice with live totals and a clear save flow.
whenToUse: Creating or editing an invoice or quote with line items.
Forms that need a live subtotal and total as quantities and rates change.
whenNotToUse: Use billing-overview to show past invoices and plan status.
Use checkout-flow when the customer is paying.
Use sortable-data-table for read-only lists of invoices.

name: journey-flow
title: Journey flow
description: A Sankey of user journeys whose flows morph by channel and trace a cohort on hover.
whenToUse: Showing where users go between funnel stages, such as visit to signup to activation.
Comparing flows across acquisition channels with a segment switch.
Tracing one step to see which paths lead into and out of it.
whenNotToUse: Use cohort-retention to show how groups retain over time.
Use bar-chart for a simple linear funnel without branching paths.
Use metrics-dashboard for a general KPI overview.

name: kanban-board
title: Kanban board
description: A kanban board where cards lift, tilt and spring into the slot that opens for them, with swimlanes and live WIP limits.
whenToUse: A team board where cards move between statuses.
Pipelines where ordering within a stage matters.
Boards that need a per person view.
whenNotToUse: Scheduling on dates; use gantt-timeline or week-calendar.
Read only status summaries; use a table.
Hundreds of cards per column; virtualize or use customers-table.

name: knowledge-base
title: Knowledge base
description: A retrieval knowledge base in one card: add sources and watch them parse, chunk, embed and index, then test a question and see which chunks come back and why.
whenToUse: Admin screens for a RAG or support assistant where people add documents, watch them index, and check what a question retrieves.
Explaining or tuning chunking, hybrid search and reranking with a working test bench instead of a diagram.
Debugging why an assistant answered from the wrong source by looking at scores, matches and neighbouring chunks.
whenNotToUse: Use vector-search to illustrate how embeddings and nearest neighbours work; this block is the working product surface.
Use document-extract to pull structured fields out of a single document.
Use agent-memory to show what an agent remembers about a user or a project.
Use ai-answer or research-run to show the cited answer a model writes from retrieved sources.

name: kpi-drilldown
title: KPI drilldown
description: KPI cards that expand into a full detail chart with period comparison and a breakdown table, then fold back.
whenToUse: An analytics or finance overview where each number deserves a closer look.
Executive dashboards that compare the current period with the previous one.
whenNotToUse: Use metric-explorer to compare many metrics on one chart.
Use metrics-dashboard for a static summary without drill down.
Avoid it for real time monitoring where values change every second.

name: layout-morph
title: Layout morph
description: A 24 card gallery that flies between grid, masonry, list, fan, carousel and a 3D helix.
whenToUse: Catalogue, portfolio, or team pages where people browse the same set in different layouts.
Showcase galleries that fly between grid, masonry, list, fan, carousel, and a 3D helix.
whenNotToUse: Use photo-grid for a simple gallery.
Use carousel or cover-flow for one horizontal browsing style.
Use lightbox-gallery when opening a full size image is the main job.

name: lead-scoring
title: Lead scoring
description: A lead scoring card where inbound B2B leads are ranked by an AI fit score, each with a score ring and a one-line reason. Open a lead to see its signals and score breakdown, then push it to HubSpot or Salesforce.
whenToUse: A sales inbox or SDR queue that ranks new inbound leads by fit.
Showing why a model scored a lead, with signals and a weighted breakdown.
Handing a qualified lead to HubSpot or Salesforce from the same view.
whenNotToUse: Large tables of hundreds of leads with filters and bulk edits; use a data table.
Enriching columns of company data; use enrich-column.
Tracking the health of existing customers; use account-health.

name: line-replay
title: Line replay
description: A time replay line chart that draws a day of traffic with a moving playhead, a value label on the tip, a scrubber, speed control and key moments annotated as the playhead passes them.
whenToUse: Post-launch or campaign reviews where the team wants to watch traffic respond to each announcement.
Incident retrospectives that step through a metric with the alert, the deploy and the recovery marked.
Storytelling pages and reports where a single series over one session or day is best understood in sequence.
whenNotToUse: Use annotated-trend when people need to add and edit their own notes on a static trend.
Use connected-scatter to replay how two measures moved together over time.
Use metric-explorer or a line chart to compare several series or ranges at a glance without playback.

name: login
title: Login and sign up
description: A glass magic link card over dusk photography that folds its envelope shut once sent.
whenToUse: A magic link sign in page with a strong brand photo behind a glass card.
Consumer or creative products where the sign in screen carries the brand mood.
whenNotToUse: Use login-centered for passkey-first auth with an email code.
Use login-split for password sign in with a quieter layout.
Use sign-in when the form sits inside an existing page.

name: magic-link
title: Magic link
description: A passwordless sign in card where an email with inline validation and typo fixes sends a magic link, and the card crossfades in place to a check your inbox step with a sealing envelope, Gmail and Outlook shortcuts and a resend countdown. Google and GitHub sign in sit above, with their real marks.
whenToUse: Passwordless sign in or sign up by email link, with optional Google and GitHub sign in.
B2B products that want a work email gate with a clear what happens next screen.
Replacing a password form to cut sign in friction and reset requests.
whenNotToUse: Password plus email sign in or MFA codes; use sign-in or a login block instead.
One time codes typed into the app; use an OTP input flow.
Full page marketing sign in layouts with imagery; use login-split.

name: market-terminal
title: Market terminal
description: A trading terminal with a canvas candlestick chart, volume, moving averages, crosshair OHLC readout, wheel, drag and pinch zoom, a live watchlist with sparklines and flashing prices, and a market and limit order ticket.
whenToUse: A trading or investing product that needs a full chart, a watchlist and an order ticket on one screen.
A paper trading or education app where people practice placing market and limit orders against moving prices.
A markets dashboard where candles, volume and moving averages must be inspected bar by bar.
whenNotToUse: Use order-book-depth to show bids and asks at each price level.
Use metric-explorer or a line chart for product or business metrics without open, high, low and close.
Use options-payoff to model an options position's profit at expiry.
Use wallet-card for a simple balance and recent transactions without a chart.

name: mcp-servers
title: MCP servers
description: Manage the MCP servers that give an agent its tools: see what the enabled tools cost in context, connect or pause a server, and switch single tools on or off.
whenToUse: Settings for an agent or AI assistant that connects to MCP servers: which servers it has, which tools are on and what they cost in context.
Onboarding a new integration with a directory, sign in and tool discovery in one place.
Keeping tool definitions inside a context budget by switching off tools the agent does not need.
whenNotToUse: Use agent-approvals to approve or deny individual tool calls while the agent runs.
Use context-window to show everything in the context window, not only tool definitions.
Use agent-run to follow an agent's steps and tool calls live.
Use knowledge-base to manage documents an agent retrieves from, rather than tools it calls.

name: media-player
title: Media player
description: An audio player with a living playlist and complete playback controls.
whenToUse: A small audio collection such as a podcast, sample pack, or playlist.
Pages that need a full player with seek, skip, volume, and a track list.
whenNotToUse: Use now-playing for a compact now playing widget.
Use transcript-studio when the audio needs a synced transcript.
Use voice-recorder for recording audio.

name: metric-explorer
title: Metric explorer
description: KPI cards that open into a scrubbable chart and morph between metrics and ranges.
whenToUse: The top of a SaaS analytics or finance page with KPI cards that open into a chart.
Dashboards where people move between a few metrics and date ranges.
whenNotToUse: Use stat-card or metric-card for static KPI tiles.
Use revenue-explorer for a revenue breakdown with a range brush.
Use metrics-dashboard for a full dashboard layout.

name: metrics-dashboard
title: Metrics dashboard
description: A dense analytics view with KPI tabs, one inspectable chart, and top pages and sources.
whenToUse: A small, explorable KPI overview with a range toggle and one chart.
Product or marketing dashboards with four headline metrics, a 7, 30, or 90 day range, and top pages and sources.
whenNotToUse: Use metric-explorer or revenue-explorer for larger or drill-down data.
Use stat-card for a single number.
Use sparkline for inline trends in a table.

name: model-arena
title: Model arena
description: A blind side by side model comparison in one card: send one prompt to two models, watch both answers stream at the same pace, vote for the better one, then reveal which model wrote each.
whenToUse: Blind human preference tests between two models on the same prompt, such as an internal bake-off before switching providers.
Prompt or model evaluation tools where people should judge answers without knowing which model wrote them.
Showing latency, speed and cost differences between two models live, side by side, on a real prompt.
whenNotToUse: Use model-picker to let someone choose one model for their own chat; this block compares answers, it does not set a default.
Use eval-suite to score many prompts automatically against expected outputs rather than collecting one human vote at a time.
Use model-router to explain or configure automatic routing between models.
Use ai-chat for a single ongoing conversation with one model.

name: model-picker
title: Model picker
description: A model picker in one quiet pill: open it to choose from featured models with a one line note each, set the reasoning effort, or browse every other model by provider, and the pill swaps to your choice in place.
whenToUse: Choosing the model and effort for a chat, an agent or a playground.
A default model setting with a short review of what the chosen model costs and how much context it takes.
whenNotToUse: Comparing two models' answers side by side; use model-arena.
A full prompt box with attachments and tools; use ai-composer, which has its own model chip.
Choosing from a plain list of options with no descriptions; use the select or dropdown-menu component.

name: mrr-waterfall
title: MRR waterfall
description: An MRR bridge whose floating bars morph by period and open the accounts behind each move.
whenToUse: Revenue or board reporting that explains how MRR moved from start to end of a period.
Finance views where each movement should list the accounts behind it.
whenNotToUse: Use revenue-explorer for MRR over many months.
Use bar-chart for plain comparisons that do not build from a start value.
Use cohort-retention for retention by cohort.

name: multi-step-form
title: Multi-step form
description: A guided form that presents one decision at a time and preserves progress.
whenToUse: Onboarding or intake flows split into a few short steps.
Wizards that need Back and Continue, progress, and a success state out of the box.
whenNotToUse: Use stepper when you only need the progress indicator.
Use checkout-flow for full page flows.
Use onboarding-checklist for tasks done outside a form.

name: onboarding-illustration
title: Onboarding illustration
description: A compact onboarding card whose line illustration morphs from folder to files, team, and badge.
whenToUse: A short first-run dialog in a document or workspace product.
Onboarding with three or four steps that each need a simple picture.
whenNotToUse: Use onboarding-checklist for tasks people complete over time.
Use feature-illustration for a feature section on a marketing page.

name: onboarding-survey
title: Onboarding survey
description: A post-signup onboarding survey where each question gets its own step of large option cards, picked with keys 1 to 4 and Enter. A short personalization checklist then ticks off and lands on an editable "You're all set" summary.
whenToUse: Post-signup personalization: role, team size and first action before the first screen.
Short in-product surveys where every answer changes what someone sees next.
Re-onboarding when a workspace changes plan or adds a team.
whenNotToUse: Long forms with free text or many fields; use a regular form or import-wizard.
Guided tours over the real interface; use onboarding-tour.
A single choice inside a settings page; use radio-cards.

name: pricing-calculator
title: Pricing calculator
description: A seat slider and billing toggle drive plan cards with rolling prices and a moving recommended badge.
whenToUse: Per-seat pricing where showing the exact total for a team size helps people choose.
Pricing pages with a monthly and yearly toggle and a visible yearly saving.
Plans with seat caps or volume discounts that are hard to explain in a static table.
whenNotToUse: Use usage-pricing when price depends on metered usage rather than seats.
Use plan-comparison for a feature by feature table across plans.
Use billing-toggle when you only need the monthly and yearly switch.

name: product-detail
title: Product detail
description: A product page with a swipeable gallery, finish and size variants, add to bag that confirms in place, shipping, a reviews summary, and details.
whenToUse: Product pages with a few variants, a gallery, and reviews.
Stores that want stock aware variants with a restock alert instead of a dead button.
whenNotToUse: Products built from many options with live pricing; use product-configurator.
Browsing many products; use product-listing.

name: product-listing
title: Product listing
description: A storefront grid with price, color and size filters, a sort menu, hover photo swaps, and quick add with a size row.
whenToUse: A shop's collection or category page with a few dozen to a few hundred products.
Catalogs where color and size are the main filters and a quick add saves a trip to the product page.
whenNotToUse: One product with many options; use product-detail or product-configurator.
Huge catalogs with faceted server search; keep the card and filter styles but fetch results from your search service.

name: profile-page
title: Profile page
description: A user profile with cover, bio, stats, activity and project tabs, and an edit sheet that writes back into the page.
whenToUse: A person's own profile with an edit flow
Public creator or member pages inside an app
Team member pages that show recent work
whenNotToUse: Account security or billing settings, use settings-page
A directory of many people, use team-directory
A marketing team section, use team-showcase

name: project-board
title: Project board
description: A living workflow board for moving work between stages.
whenToUse: A compact kanban with a handful of tasks across fixed stages.
Boards where moving tasks should be accessible through explicit buttons, not drag only.
whenNotToUse: Use reorderable-list when order within one list matters more than stages.
Use timeline for a dated sequence of events.
Add drag and drop and virtualization, or use a dedicated board library, for large boards.

name: prompt-studio
title: Prompt studio
description: One card for editing, testing and shipping a prompt template: variables as chips with sample values, a test run against the chosen model, and versions you can compare and promote to production.
whenToUse: A settings or admin page where a support lead or engineer tunes the prompt behind one AI feature and tests it on real cases.
Prompt management that needs a compact version history with authors, a diff against an earlier version and a visible production pointer.
Any LLM feature with template variables filled from records, such as a support reply, a summary or a classifier prompt.
whenNotToUse: Use ai-chat for an end user conversation; this card edits templates, not messages.
Use model-arena to compare the replies of several models side by side on one prompt.
Use eval-suite to score a prompt across many cases with graders and pass rates.
Use model-picker when the only job is choosing a model and effort.

name: release-readiness
title: Release readiness
description: A launch checklist that keeps prerequisites, progress, and the final action together.
whenToUse: A pre-launch or handoff gate where several checks must be done before one action unlocks.
Release or launch checklists with a readiness bar and owners.
Handoffs that should optionally notify people when the action runs.
whenNotToUse: Use onboarding-checklist for a user's own getting-started tasks.

name: research-run
title: Research run
description: Deep research that plans searches, reads sources with their marks, and streams a cited answer where every chip lights up the sentence it supports.
whenToUse: An answer engine or deep research feature that searches, reads and cites.
Internal knowledge search where people must verify each claim.
Any long streamed answer that benefits from visible sources and follow ups.
whenNotToUse: Open ended conversation without sources; use ai-chat.
An agent that edits files or runs tools; use agent-run.
A single answer with sources inside another page; use ai-answer.

name: revenue-explorer
title: Revenue explorer
description: A SaaS revenue chart you zoom with a brush while paths, axes and figures glide to the range.
whenToUse: Monthly MRR or revenue broken into new, expansion, and churn on an analytics page.
Charts where people need to zoom a date range with an overview brush and compare against a prior period.
whenNotToUse: Use mrr-waterfall to explain how MRR moved between two points in time.
Use metric-explorer for a row of KPI cards that open into a chart.
Use bar-chart or sparkline for a small chart inside a card.

name: revenue-globe
title: Revenue globe
description: A dotted globe where live payments arc home to headquarters, with a replayable day.
whenToUse: Revenue or operations overviews showing where payments come from right now.
Showcase pages where a live globe with arcs and a day timeline adds impact.
whenNotToUse: Use a table or bar-chart when exact regional numbers matter more than the view.
Use customer-galaxy to explore accounts rather than transactions.
Use revenue-explorer for revenue over time.

name: roles-permissions
title: Roles and permissions
description: A permissions matrix with group toggles that ripple, role duplication and a review bar.
whenToUse: Workspace settings where admins edit what each role can do.
Permission matrices with grouped permissions and a review step before saving.
whenNotToUse: Use team-members to assign roles to people.
Use switch rows in settings-page for a few on and off settings.
Use security-settings for personal account security.

name: scroll-story
title: Scroll story
description: A feature section where scrolling the copy drives a pinned product view through each step.
whenToUse: Marketing pages that walk through a product in a few steps as people scroll.
Feature sections where a pinned product view should change with the copy.
whenNotToUse: Use scroll-highlight for a single paragraph that reveals with scroll.
Use chaos-to-order for one before and after switch.
Use feature-illustration for a static feature visual.

name: search-results
title: Search results
description: A faceted workspace search page with suggestions, facet counts that follow the query, filter chips, mixed doc, person and file results with highlighted matches, a gliding keyboard cursor and a preview pane.
whenToUse: A full search page for a workspace or knowledge base that returns several kinds of things at once.
Search where people narrow by type, team, and date, and want to read a match before opening it.
whenNotToUse: Use command-palette for quick jump to navigation from any screen.
Use product-listing for a storefront grid filtered by price, color, and size.
Use customers-table or sortable-data-table when results are records to compare in columns.

name: seat-manager
title: Seat manager
description: A team seats and billing card where avatars and a seat meter show members, invites and open seats against what you pay for, a stepper rolls the prorated charge for today and the new monthly total live, and changes go through a confirm step before anyone is charged. Pending invites can be resent or revoked with undo, and when every seat is taken the card says so and offers to add one.
whenToUse: Letting a team admin add or remove paid seats with the price impact visible before paying.
Showing seat usage against purchased seats, including invites that reserve a seat.
Handling the seat limit at the moment an admin hits it, with a one tap way to add a seat.
whenNotToUse: Managing roles and permissions for many members: use a member table and link to this card for seats.
Usage based or credit billing: use credit-topup or a usage meter instead.
Plan comparison or upgrades between tiers: use a pricing table.

name: seat-map
title: Seat map
description: An event seat picker with a curved concert hall map, price tiers, zoom and pan, sold, held and wheelchair seats, and a live summary with fees and a hold countdown.
whenToUse: Reserved seating for concerts, theatre, sports and conferences where the buyer picks exact seats.
Any spatial picker with priced places: tables in a restaurant plan, desks in an office, cabins on a deck.
Checkout flows that need a live total and a short hold before payment.
whenNotToUse: Use a quantity stepper with best available when seats are general admission or assigned by the box office.
Use availability-picker for choosing times rather than places.
Use choropleth-explorer to compare values across regions without selecting them.

name: security-settings
title: Security settings
description: An account security page with guided two-factor setup, password change and active sessions.
whenToUse: The security tab of account settings with two-factor setup, password change, and sessions.
Guided TOTP setup that walks through scan, verify, and backup codes.
whenNotToUse: Use settings-page for general account and workspace settings.
Use api-keys for managing developer tokens.
Use audit-log for the history of security events.

name: selection-toolbar
title: Selection toolbar
description: A contextual batch action surface that appears when items are selected.
whenToUse: Bulk actions for checkbox-selectable tables or grids.
Floating bars that appear only while items are selected.
whenNotToUse: Use dropdown-menu for per-row actions.

name: semantic-zoom
title: Semantic zoom
description: An infinite-zoom map of a company that reveals teams, projects, tasks and people as you fly in.
whenToUse: Workspace or portfolio overviews where people zoom from the whole company to one task.
Hierarchical data where each zoom level should show different detail.
whenNotToUse: Use tree-view for a plain hierarchy people scan and expand.
Use project-board for working on tasks.
Use customer-galaxy for flat data clustered by attributes.

name: settings-command
title: Settings command
description: Workspace settings where a search field grows into a palette that flies you to any setting.
whenToUse: Workspace or account settings with several sections and many options.
Admin consoles where support links people to a specific setting.
Any settings page where people ask where something lives.
whenNotToUse: Use settings-page for a short, paged profile form with a few fields per section.
Use command-palette for app wide navigation and actions, not just settings.
Avoid it for a single form; a plain form with a submit button is clearer.

name: settings-page
title: Settings page
description: Account settings with a gliding section nav and a save bar that morphs in as you edit.
whenToUse: Account or workspace settings with several sections.
Forms that should show a save bar only when something changed.
Settings where Cmd or Ctrl+S should save.
whenNotToUse: Use security-settings for sessions, two factor, and passwords.
Use billing-overview for plan and invoice management.
Use team-members for inviting and managing people.

name: sidebar
title: Sidebar
description: A product sidebar with a workspace switcher, live search, draggable favorites, and inline projects.
whenToUse: The main navigation of a multi-workspace app.
Sidebars with draggable favorites and inline project creation.
Navigation that should collapse to an icon rail with the [ shortcut.
whenNotToUse: Use sidebar-rail when you need the whole app shell with a mobile sheet.
Use docs-sidebar for documentation trees.
Use inbox-sidebar for mail folders and labels.

name: small-multiples
title: Small multiples
description: A trellis of small line charts that reads as one chart, with a synced crosshair, a shared or independent y scale that springs the axes, sorting with a FLIP reorder, a ghost of the overall total behind every panel and dimming for flat trends.
whenToUse: Comparing revenue, signups or usage across regions, products, plans or channels over the same months.
Showing which segments grow, shrink or stall at a glance, with one shared crosshair to read every value for the same period.
Dashboards where one multi-line chart would be a tangle of overlapping series.
whenNotToUse: Use line-chart when two or three series need to be read against each other on one plot.
Use metric-explorer or kpi-drilldown when a person picks one metric and drills into its detail.
Use sparkline inside a table row when each series is a small supporting detail beside other columns.
Use a plain table when the exact values matter more than the shape of each trend.

name: smart-scheduler
title: Smart scheduler
description: A scheduling card where one sentence like "Find 30 min with Maya and Leo next week, mornings" is read into chips. The three best slots are then ranked across everyone's Google Calendar and Outlook calendars, with an availability strip per person and conflicts called out. Picking a slot opens a draft invite with a Google Meet link, ready to send.
whenToUse: A scheduling assistant inside a CRM, recruiting tool, or team app that books internal meetings from one sentence.
Showing why a time was suggested: who is free, what conflicts, and what is tentative.
An AI feature demo where the result has to be checkable at a glance before anything is sent.
whenNotToUse: Public booking pages where guests pick from your open times; use availability-picker or booking-pill.
Browsing or editing a full calendar; use week-calendar or month-calendar.
Picking a single date or time without other people involved; use date-picker or time-picker.

name: spend-alert
title: Spend alert
description: A budget and spend alert card where the threshold is set right on the live spend bar, with forecast, Email, Slack and PagerDuty toggles, a hard stop and a live preview of the Slack message the alert will post.
whenToUse: Letting a team set a monthly budget and alert threshold for metered spend.
Showing how close current and forecast spend are to an alert line.
Choosing where cost alerts go and previewing the Slack message before saving.
whenNotToUse: Read-only usage reporting with no settings; use usage-forecast or usage-billing instead.
Per-seat plans with no metered spend.
Complex multi-budget policies across many projects; use a table of budgets that opens this card per row.

name: spotlight-grid
title: Spotlight grid
description: A feature grid where light follows the pointer, cards play live demos, and a click morphs a card into its detail.
whenToUse: A product landing page section that shows four features with live, hands-on previews.
Developer tool marketing where a small working demo explains a feature better than copy.
Pages that want a bento grid with one wide card per row and a detail view that opens in place.
whenNotToUse: Use use-case-gallery for a browsable set of customer or use case stories.
Use expandable-card when you need a single card that expands, not a whole feature grid.
Use feature-illustration for one static feature explained with an illustration.

name: support-conversation
title: Support conversation
description: A responsive message thread with useful quick replies and live feedback.
whenToUse: A support chat or ticket thread with quick replies and attachments.
Help flows that should show a typing indicator and a resolve toggle.
whenNotToUse: Use support-widget for a floating help launcher.
Use ai-composer for a prompt input without a thread.
Use inbox-triage to handle many conversations at once.

name: support-widget
title: Support widget
description: An in-app help launcher that grows into live article search, reading, and a chat with your team.
whenToUse: An in-app help launcher with article search, an article reader, and chat.
SaaS products that want one help entry point mounted near the app root.
whenNotToUse: Use support-conversation for a full page support chat.
Use ai-composer for an AI prompt input without help articles.
Use popover for a small anchored tip.

name: task-breakdown
title: Task breakdown
description: A goal input where AI breaks one sentence into a plan: tasks stream in with estimates, owners and dependencies, and a live timeline shows whether the deadline holds. Reorder, edit or regenerate any task, then send the plan to Linear or Jira with progress for each issue and links.
whenToUse: Turning a goal or brief into a scoped project plan inside a PM, CRM or internal tool.
Exporting AI drafted work to Linear or Jira with a review step before anything is created.
Showing whether a plan fits a deadline and updating that as people edit estimates.
whenNotToUse: Showing an agent working through steps live; use agent-plan.
A full backlog or board with many projects; use a dedicated table or kanban.
Single task creation from a prompt; a simple composer is lighter.

name: team-directory
title: Team directory
description: Searchable people, team filters, and a focused profile panel.
whenToUse: An internal directory where people search colleagues and copy contact details.
Team pages with department filters and a profile pane.
whenNotToUse: Use team-members to manage roles and invitations.
Use team-showcase for a public, image-led team section.
Use customers-table for large tabular people data.

name: team-members
title: Team members
description: A members list where typed emails turn into chips and fly into pending invites as seats roll.
whenToUse: The team or workspace settings page of a SaaS app.
Inviting several people at once by typing or pasting emails.
Member lists with roles, pending invites, and seat counts.
whenNotToUse: Use team-directory for a browsable people directory.
Use roles-permissions to define what each role can do.
Use tag-input for a general chip input outside invites.

name: team-showcase
title: Team showcase
description: An image led team introduction with profiles that open in place.
whenToUse: About or company pages that introduce the team with portraits.
Sections that need one of four layouts: gallery, filmstrip, directory, or spotlight.
whenNotToUse: Use team-directory for an internal, searchable people list.
Use team-members for managing members and roles.
Use testimonial-stage for quotes from customers.

name: testimonial-stage
title: Studio perspectives
description: Portrait led editorial stories with a focused reading state.
whenToUse: Testimonials or editorial stories where the person's portrait matters.
Landing sections that rotate through a few quotes on demand.
whenNotToUse: Use logo-marquee when logos are enough social proof.
Use carousel for many short testimonials.
Use team-showcase to introduce your own team.

name: two-factor-setup
title: Two-factor setup
description: A two-factor setup card where you scan a real, working authenticator QR code, type the 6-digit code into slots that move to the next box on their own, and save your backup codes before it turns on. Every step shares one fixed-size card, so it moves between steps with a short slide and never changes size.
whenToUse: Turning on authenticator app two-factor from account or workspace security settings.
Enforced two-factor onboarding for admins after sign-in.
Re-enrolling a new phone, with fresh backup codes.
whenNotToUse: SMS or email one-time codes only: use otp-input in a sign-in form.
Passkeys or WebAuthn enrolment, which needs no QR or code step.
A full security settings page with sessions and password: use security-settings.

name: uptime-status
title: Uptime status
description: A status page with 90 day uptime bars, a morphing latency chart and an incident timeline.
whenToUse: A public or internal status page with per-service uptime history.
Pages that combine 90 day uptime strips, response time, and an incident timeline.
whenNotToUse: Use activity-heatmap for activity counts rather than availability.
Use timeline for an incident history on its own.
Use sparkline for a small latency trend inside a card.

name: usage-billing
title: Usage billing
description: A usage based billing dashboard with a projected spend line, meters against limits, alerts, and an upgrade that morphs into a confirm sheet.
whenToUse: A billing page for usage priced SaaS or infrastructure products.
Admin dashboards where finance needs spend alerts and invoice history in one place.
Upgrade moments driven by limits, where the upgrade should explain what changes.
whenNotToUse: Use billing-overview for flat seat based plans without meters.
Use plan-comparison or usage-pricing on a public pricing page.
Avoid it for a single quota; a usage meter component is enough.

name: usage-forecast
title: Usage forecast
description: A billing period usage chart with a forecast cone and a draggable budget that dates the crossing.
whenToUse: Billing or usage pages that warn customers before they hit a budget.
Metered products that show month to date usage with a forecast range.
whenNotToUse: Use usage-meter for a simple progress bar against a limit.
Use usage-pricing to estimate price from usage before buying.
Use metric-explorer for general KPIs without a budget.

name: usage-pricing
title: Usage pricing
description: A pricing calculator that finds your plan as you drag seats and traffic.
whenToUse: Pricing pages for plans priced by seats plus usage.
Calculators that should recommend a plan as people move sliders.
Monthly and yearly toggles where the saving should be visible in the breakdown.
whenNotToUse: Use plan-comparison for a side by side table of fixed tiers.
Use usage-forecast to project spend for an existing customer.
Use billing-overview for the settings page of someone already subscribed.

name: wallet-card
title: Wallet card
description: A compact account view with balance, recent activity, and focused money actions.
whenToUse: A personal or business balance summary with quick send, deposit, swap, and buy actions.
Dashboards that pair a balance with a small history chart and recent activity.
Apps with a main and a reserve account shown in one card.
whenNotToUse: Use billing-overview for subscription billing and invoices.
Use wallet-stack for a stack of payment cards.
Use checkout-flow for paying for an order.

name: webhook-tester
title: Webhook tester
description: A developer webhook tester where you pick an event, edit its JSON payload and send a signed test event. You watch it go from signed to sent to 200 OK in 184 ms, then read the response body, headers and exact request, and retry failed deliveries from a recent list.
whenToUse: A developer settings page where customers test a webhook endpoint before going live.
Integration onboarding that asks people to prove their handler returns 2xx and verifies signatures.
Internal tools for replaying failed deliveries with a retry.
whenNotToUse: Managing many endpoints, filters and event subscriptions: use the webhooks block and link here for testing one.
A general HTTP client for arbitrary methods and headers: this always sends a signed POST with a JSON body.
Live event logs with thousands of rows: the list is for a few recent attempts, not a paginated log.

name: webhooks
title: Webhooks
description: A webhooks console with delivery history, a payload inspector and retries that roll the rate.
whenToUse: A developer settings page for webhook endpoints, delivery history, and retries.
Consoles that need a payload and headers inspector next to the delivery list.
whenNotToUse: Use api-keys for managing tokens.
Use audit-log for account activity rather than outgoing events.
Use integrations for a catalogue of third-party connections.

name: week-calendar
title: Week calendar
description: A week calendar where you drag to create, move, and resize events, with color coded calendars, day and agenda views, and swipes on phones.
whenToUse: Scheduling and planning screens where people create, move and resize time blocks across a week.
Team or personal calendars that need several color coded calendars, all day events and an agenda on phones.
whenNotToUse: Use month-calendar for a month overview with events per day.
Use calendar or date-picker to pick a date, and time-picker for a single time.
Use availability-picker to collect open slots from someone.

name: action-morph
title: Action morph
description: A floating button that morphs into a quick-action menu, then an inline form, then back with a check.
whenToUse: Quick capture of tasks, notes, or comments without leaving the page.
Apps with a few frequent create actions that deserve a persistent button.
Mobile layouts where a corner button should expand into a small form.
whenNotToUse: Use dialog or drawer for longer forms with several fields.
Use dropdown-menu when actions run immediately and need no input.
Use action-button for one async save on a button in place.

name: activity-rings
title: Activity rings
description: Daily goals as tick rings that sweep, count up, and trace a second lap past 100%.
whenToUse: Daily goals that fill up and can be exceeded, like move, exercise, and stand.
Fitness or habit dashboards with a week picker to compare days.
whenNotToUse: Use progress or gauge for a single value.
Use usage-meter for quotas and limits.
Use activity-heatmap for streaks across many weeks.

name: agent-cursor
title: Agent cursor
description: A live document where Claude edits like a collaborator. Its labeled cursor comes out of its avatar, selects a paragraph and streams in a rewrite, adds a heading and fixes a typo, while a teammate's cursor reads along. Changes stay tinted until someone accepts or undoes them from a floating review bar.
whenToUse: Showing an AI writing assistant that edits a doc alongside people, with accept and undo.
Landing or onboarding sections that demo a collaborative AI editor in motion.
A product surface that streams structured edits from an agent and needs a human review step.
whenNotToUse: Free form chat or Q&A: use a chat transcript component.
A real rich text editor: wire your editor's own collaboration cursors; this card renders read-only blocks.
Long documents with many sections: the card is built for a short excerpt of five to ten blocks.

name: agent-handoff
title: Agent handoff
description: A support conversation where an AI assistant hands off to a person. When it transfers, a card shows the summary it passes to the team and the typical wait. The person then joins and takes over, and a thin timeline on the left marks each step.
whenToUse: A support widget where the AI answers first and escalates to a human agent.
Showing customers what the assistant shared with the team, so they do not repeat themselves.
Marketing or docs pages that explain an AI to human handoff flow.
whenNotToUse: A general chat with one assistant and no handoff: use chat-thread.
Showing an agent's internal steps or tool calls: use agent-timeline or tool-call.
A full help desk inbox for agents: build it from list and detail layouts instead.

name: agent-loop
title: Agent loop
description: An illustration of the agent loop: gather context, take action, verify, repeat, with a bright head circling three stations around the model.
whenToUse: Docs, explainers and landing pages that teach how an AI agent works: it gathers context, calls tools, checks the result and repeats until the task is done.
Showing why agents take several passes, with a failed check or a failed tool call that sends the loop round again.
A visual summary of a finished agent run with the tools it used and the context it built up.
whenNotToUse: Use agent-run or research-run to show a real agent's live steps and streamed output.
Use tool-call for a single tool call card inside a chat or a log.
Use reasoning-tree to explain search over thoughts rather than tool use.
Use mcp-flow to explain how a host talks to MCP servers over a transport.
Use context-window to show what fills a model's context and how close it is to the limit.

name: agent-plan
title: Agent plan
description: The plan an agent writes before it acts: edit, reorder or add steps while it is a draft, then watch it work through them as a live checklist.
whenToUse: An agent should show and get approval for its plan before it edits code, runs commands or touches production.
A person needs to adjust the agent's plan (rename, reorder, remove or add steps) and then watch the same plan execute.
A side panel or chat message that tracks a multi-step task with a live current step, failures that need a decision, and a final summary.
whenNotToUse: Use agent-run for a streaming transcript of everything the agent did, with tool calls and output, rather than a checklist of steps.
Use agent-approvals when the person approves individual risky actions one at a time instead of a whole plan up front.
Use agent-tasks for a queue of independent tasks across agents rather than one ordered plan.
Use research-run for search and reading progress that ends in a cited answer.

name: agent-status
title: Agent status
description: A compact live status pill for a running AI agent: the agent's mark in a live ring, the current activity and an elapsed timer, opening into the steps so far.
whenToUse: An app header, title bar or composer that needs to show at a glance that an agent is running, what it is doing and for how long.
Coding, research or browser agents that pause for approval, so the person can approve or deny without opening a full run view.
Background runs that people check on occasionally: the pill stays small, and the panel shows recent steps and controls on demand.
whenNotToUse: Use agent-run or research-run when the run itself is the page and every step, tool call and output needs room.
Use agent-approvals to review a queue of pending approvals across several agents.
Use agent-orchestrator or agent-tasks to compare many agents or runs at once.
Use text-shimmer alone for a single inline working label without a timer, steps or controls.

name: agent-timeline
title: Agent timeline
description: A compact timeline of one orchestrated agent run: the orchestrator and its subagents share a time axis, handoffs draw in between rows, and a playhead replays thinking, tool calls and waiting while the header counts time, tokens and cost. Hover a span for what it did, or click it to trace its handoff path.
whenToUse: Showing how an orchestrator split work across subagents and how long each part took, in a run history, a trace viewer or a debugging panel.
Replaying a finished agent run in a product demo or changelog, with real numbers for time, tokens and cost.
Following a multi-agent run live as events stream in from your backend.
whenNotToUse: Use agent-orchestrator for a full screen of agent lanes with streaming text and messages; this timeline is the compact, reusable view of timing.
Use observability-trace for distributed request tracing across services rather than agents.
Use agent-run or research-run when people need the agent's steps, sources and answer, not the timing.
Use tool-call for the detail of a single tool invocation, and agent-status for one agent's current state.

name: ai-command
title: AI command
description: A Cmd+K command palette with an AI mode. Search pages and actions, or press Tab to ask a question: the answer streams inside the palette with numbered sources, and the next steps it suggests, like filing a Linear issue or opening a Notion doc, run straight from the list.
whenToUse: A global Cmd+K in a SaaS app where people both jump to pages and ask questions about their workspace.
Search that should fall back to an AI answer when nothing matches.
Answers that lead straight to an action in another tool, like filing a Linear issue or posting to Slack.
whenNotToUse: A long, multi-turn conversation: use a chat thread.
Plain navigation with no AI: use command-palette.
Inline field suggestions while typing in a form: use an autocomplete input.

name: ai-mascot
title: AI mascot
description: A small assistant character, a soft pebble with pill eyes and a companion dot, that shows what the AI is doing. It breathes and glances when idle, leans in to listen, looks up while the dot orbits its head, reads along the line it writes, squints with a sparkle when done and shakes once with worried brows on an error.
whenToUse: Give an assistant a face that shows what it is doing: in a reply header, beside a composer, on an image canvas while it generates, or in an empty state.
Products that want generation to feel alive and friendly without a spinner, with states that read at 24px.
whenNotToUse: Use agent-status when people need the steps, tools and elapsed time of a run, not just a mood.
Use text-shimmer alone for a plain "Thinking" line in dense interfaces where a character would distract.
Do not use it as a progress indicator with a known percentage; use a progress bar.

name: ai-spark
title: AI spark
description: A brand-quality animated spark mark. Four tapered rays and four lighter diagonals breathe at rest, ripple while thinking, pulse like a heartbeat while writing, then gather and settle when done. Every status change blends from the pose the mark is already in.
whenToUse: Showing that an assistant is thinking or writing, inline above a streaming reply.
A send or generate button that turns into a working indicator inside a composer.
An image or canvas tool that needs a calm, branded working mark over the canvas while a render runs.
Empty states and onboarding where a 64 to 96px hero mark gives the AI feature an identity.
whenNotToUse: Determinate progress with a known percentage; use a progress bar or the generation stats component instead.
Multi step agent runs where each step needs its own state and detail; use agent-status or agent-run.
Plain text loading lines with no mark; use text-shimmer.

name: ai-translate
title: AI translate
description: A message card where picking a language streams the AI translation in place, sentence by sentence over the dimmed original, with a detected-language chip, a Show original toggle and a status line credited to the model's mark.
whenToUse: Messages, comments, reviews or support tickets written in another language, translated on demand inside the product.
Release notes or announcements that readers in several regions open in their own language.
Any place you want an AI translation to feel inline and reversible, with the original one click away.
whenNotToUse: Translating a whole page or app interface; use your i18n framework.
Long documents with headings and lists; this renders one plain paragraph.
Live captions or speech; use a realtime stream component.

name: ai-workflow
title: AI workflow
description: A Linear-style AI workflow card where a Gmail trigger, a Claude step, a branch and Slack and Linear actions sit on one hairline rail, and a test run glides down it, opening each step's output inline. Steps are added from a compact command menu with real app marks.
