whenToUse: An automation or integrations page where people assemble a short trigger, AI step and action flow and want to test it in place.
Onboarding or marketing surfaces that show how an AI step slots between real apps, with a working test run.
Reviewing what an existing workflow does and seeing a sample run's outputs step by step.
whenNotToUse: Large free-form graphs with many branches, loops or merges: use a canvas editor instead.
Showing a single tool call or a live agent's steps: use tool-call or agent-run.
Scheduling recurring agent jobs: use agent-routines.

name: ask-your-data
title: Ask your data
description: A natural language to chart card: you ask a question, PostgreSQL streams into a collapsible, syntax highlighted panel, the query runs with a rolling row count, and the answer builds as stacked bars, lines or a table, with a one line insight streamed in underneath.
whenToUse: Letting people ask product or business questions in plain words and see a chart, with the SQL one click away to verify or copy.
Embedding an analytics answer in a dashboard card, an admin page or an AI assistant's result view.
Teaching or auditing text to SQL, where showing the generated query builds trust.
whenNotToUse: Use bar-chart or line-chart when the query is fixed and there is no question to ask.
Use tool-call to show a database query as one step inside a longer agent transcript.
Use sql-editor when people write and tune queries by hand.

name: avatar-upload
title: Avatar upload
description: Click or drop a photo onto the avatar to crop it in place with drag, pinch and zoom. It uploads through a progress ring and settles, with clear errors and retry.
whenToUse: Profile, account and team member settings where a person sets their own photo.
Workspace or organization logos that display in a circle.
Onboarding steps that ask for a photo and should show upload progress in place.
whenNotToUse: Several files or documents at once: use file-dropzone.
Free form crops with aspect ratios, rotation or a large canvas: use image-cropper.
Showing an avatar without editing: use avatar.

name: black-hole
title: Black hole
description: A delete transition that pulls the chosen items into a tiny singularity while the rest of the list bends around it; undo spins them back out.
whenToUse: Deleting or archiving a handful of selected rows, cards, or files, with an Undo right after.
Emptying a trash, clearing notifications, or dismissing a batch where the removal should feel final.
whenNotToUse: High frequency deletes such as clearing a single chip or tag. Use a quick height collapse instead.
Irreversible actions without undo. The spectacle should not stand in for a confirmation.
Very long lists that scroll; the effect paints the visible wrapper, so wrap only the scrolling viewport.

name: booking-pill
title: Booking pill
description: One pill that reshapes through party size, date, time, and a ticket.
whenToUse: Venue or service pages where booking a table or slot is the one action people came for.
Mobile-first flows that walk through party size, date, time, and confirm in one surface.
whenNotToUse: Use date-picker and time-picker inside a regular form for multi-field checkouts.
Use stepper or multi-step-form for longer flows with many fields.
Use calendar when people need to see a whole month.

name: branch-graph
title: Branch graph
description: A git commit graph where branches draw in as colored lanes, merge commits join lines, a rebase lifts commits and replays them onto main, a squash folds them into one, and hovering a commit shows its message, author and diff stats.
whenToUse: A merge strategy picker in a code review or pull request screen, showing exactly what main will look like afterwards.
A commit history panel in a developer tool, with hover details and keyboard browsing.
Docs and landing pages for version control or CI products that explain merge, rebase, and squash.
whenNotToUse: Use git-branches for a looping, non-interactive illustration of a branch, pull request, and release.
Use a timeline or changelog for releases people need to read rather than a commit graph.
Use a virtualized table for long real histories; this graph is built for a focused slice of about five to fifteen commits.

name: card-to-article
title: Card to article
description: Story cards that open into full articles with one seamless morph and shrink back into their exact slot when dragged down.
whenToUse: Blogs, journals, and changelogs where each entry has a strong image.
Case study and portfolio grids.
Editorial landing sections that preview stories without leaving the page.
whenNotToUse: Use a normal link to a page when articles are long or need their own URL and SEO.
Use expandable-card for small inline details.
Text only lists with no imagery.

name: code-suggestion
title: Code suggestion
description: An AI code edit suggestion where the model's proposed changes stream into a small editor panel as inline diff hunks, and you accept or reject each one, or all at once with Cmd+Enter. Accepted hunks fold into the file with a smooth height change.
whenToUse: Showing an AI's proposed edit to a file as an inline diff the person accepts or rejects hunk by hunk.
Approving an agent's file change before it is written, with a clear record of what was kept.
Landing pages and docs that demonstrate an AI coding feature with a realistic, self playing edit.
whenNotToUse: Use a dedicated diff tool for large multi file diffs or side by side comparisons; this card is for one file and a handful of hunks.
Use code-magic-move to animate code from one version to another without a review step.
Use code-block to show code without changes.
Use tool-call for an agent step that is not a file edit.
Use agent-approvals when the person approves actions in general (emails, payments, deploys) rather than code.

name: confirm-popover
title: Confirm popover
description: A destructive button that grows into a small confirmation card, with the consequence, optional type-to-confirm, progress on the Confirm button, and a check or error before folding back.
whenToUse: A danger zone in settings: delete project, transfer ownership, revoke a member.
A row action in a table where a modal would lose the row's context.
Any destructive action that needs a sentence of consequence and a visible result without leaving the page.
whenNotToUse: Reversible removals such as archiving; use undo-toast so the action is instant and recoverable.
A one word inline confirmation in a toolbar; use confirm-morph, which morphs horizontally inside the button's row.
Long forms or several decisions; use dialog.

name: connector-setup
title: Connector setup
description: A "Connect your tools" card for an AI assistant. Each app connects inline: it redirects, authorizes and runs a first sync with a progress hairline, then lists the scopes it was granted and offers Disconnect with an inline confirm.
whenToUse: An assistant's settings or onboarding step where people connect workspace apps.
A first-run checklist that needs to show the OAuth handshake and first sync inline, without leaving the page.
Reviewing which scopes an assistant holds per app and revoking them.
whenNotToUse: Browsing dozens of integrations by category: use the integrations-grid block.
Approving a single action the agent wants to take: use agent-approvals.
Showing a tool the agent is calling right now: use tool-call.

name: context-window
title: Context window
description: An AI context window as a grid of 200 cells: the system prompt, tools, files, summary and messages fill it in order, a threshold row marks where compaction starts, and sending a message, attaching a file or compacting shows exactly how much still fits.
whenToUse: Showing developers or power users what fills a model's context and when it will compact.
Agent and coding tools that compact long sessions and want the effect to be understandable.
Docs and onboarding that explain context windows, compaction and output reserves.
whenNotToUse: A simple quota or plan usage bar; use usage-meter.
Choosing a model; use model-picker.
Billing or spend over time; use usage-billing.

name: control-center
title: Control center
description: Workspace quick settings: tiles that morph into detail, a duration dial, and rubber-banded meters.
whenToUse: A quick settings panel with a handful of toggles and levels for a web workspace.
Focus session controls with a duration dial and allowed people.
Notification channel toggles grouped behind one tile.
whenNotToUse: Use switch, slider, and radio-group directly in a regular settings form.
Use time-dial to pick a time across time zones.
Use dropdown-menu for a short list of commands.

name: cover-flow
title: Cover flow
description: A depth rail of images you can throw, with soft grounded shadows and a quiet reflection.
whenToUse: Six to twelve visual items where looking at one at a time is the point, such as albums, places, or collections.
Showcase rails that should respond to drag, throw, and sideways trackpad scroll.
whenNotToUse: Use carousel for general slides or content cards.
Use photo-grid or lightbox-gallery for a large library.
Use depth-cards for about three rich choices that open into detail.

name: cube-mascot
title: Cube mascot
description: An isometric cube mascot where three shaded faces and a painted-on face show what the assistant is doing. It turns a quarter turn in eased steps while thinking, prints lines onto the floor while writing, settles with a sparkle when done, and shakes once on error.
whenToUse: Give an assistant a recognisable, product-like character that shows it is generating: in a reply header, in a composer, on an image canvas or in an empty state.
Brands with a geometric, technical feel where a soft blob would feel off.
whenNotToUse: Use ai-mascot for a softer, rounder character, or when you need a listening state.
Use agent-status when people need the steps, tools and elapsed time of a run.
Do not use it as a progress indicator with a known percentage; use a progress bar.

name: data-flow
title: Data flow
description: Data flow illustration. Sources (app, database, events) are on the left, a processing core with a live count sits in the middle, and destinations (warehouse, dashboard, alerts) are on the right. Records leave as hollow dots and travel curved paths. In the core they turn into solid accent squares, then fan out to each destination; alerts receives about every third record.
whenToUse: A hero or feature section explaining how data moves through a product.
Docs pages introducing an ingestion, transform, or routing concept.
Integration pages that show which sources feed which destinations.
whenNotToUse: Use sankey-flow to show real volumes between stages.
Use pipeline-status for the live state of a CI or data job.
Use a table or list when people need to act on individual records.

name: data-grid
title: Data grid
description: A spreadsheet grid with range selection, inline editing, a fill handle, and animated sorting.
whenToUse: Editing many values in place like a spreadsheet, such as budgets, price lists, or inventory.
Data people move to and from Excel or Google Sheets with copy and paste.
Work that needs range selection, a fill handle, fill down, and undo.
Large tables, up to tens of thousands of rows, that people filter, sort, group with subtotals, and total.
Server data too large to send at once, loaded in blocks as people scroll through a dataSource.
Finance tables with many period columns, date columns, and exports people open in Excel.
Bulk work on checked rows: copy, CSV export, delete, or your own actions.
whenNotToUse: Use sortable-data-table for read-only records with sorting and row selection.
Use a form when people edit one record at a time.
Use a card list or card grid when each record needs rich content like images or long text.

name: date-reel
title: Date reel
description: A 3D wheel date and time picker (like iOS reels) with momentum scrolling, snapping, curved perspective, and full keyboard support.
whenToUse: Scheduling a send, reminder or post where a phone-style wheel is familiar and faster than a calendar grid.
Touch-first flows and mobile web, where flicking a reel beats typing a date.
Birthdays and other dates far from today, using date mode with its month, day and year reels.
whenNotToUse: Use date-picker or date-range-picker when people need to see a whole month or pick a range.
Use time-picker for a compact field inside a dense form.
Use time-dial to compare times across cities.

name: dictation-button
title: Dictation button
description: A chat composer with voice input, where the mic springs into a recording pill with a smooth live waveform, a timer, and cancel and insert buttons. Words stream into the field as you speak, muted until the recognizer settles them.
whenToUse: Chat and agent composers where people would rather talk than type: mobile, long prompts, accessibility.
Notes, comments and support replies where dictation saves time and the person still edits before sending.
Any field that already has a send action and needs a voice entry point with clear listening state.
whenNotToUse: Full duplex voice conversations with spoken replies; use a voice agent pattern with call controls instead.
Recording audio files to keep (voice memos); this inserts text and discards audio.
Command palettes where a single spoken command should run immediately; confirm hands-free from onSpeechEnd only if you are sure.

name: dns-resolution
title: DNS resolution
description: A browser asks for a domain and the query hops from the resolver to a root server, the TLD server and the authoritative nameserver, each pointing to the next, until an IP address comes back and the page connects. The resolver keeps the answer with a TTL ring that drains, and a second lookup is answered straight from that cache in one short hop.
whenToUse: A docs or marketing section that explains how a domain name turns into an address and why the second visit is faster.
Custom domain setup, DNS hosting, resolver or CDN pages that need the chain of servers and the role of TTL to click.
Teaching material where viewers should be able to step back and forth through each hop.
whenNotToUse: Use webhook-fanout to show one event delivered to many endpoints with retries.
Use data-flow for a general pipeline between services.
Use a real status or table component to report actual DNS records or propagation.

name: dock
title: Dock
description: A floating tool dock with a gliding label, a springy selection, and trays that grow out of it.
whenToUse: A floating tool or mode switcher, such as the tools of a canvas or whiteboard editor.
Toolbars where related tools share one slot and open a tray, like shape variants.
Tool sets people may reorder by drag or Alt with the arrow keys.
whenNotToUse: Use segmented-control for two to four inline options.
Use action-button for one-off actions that do not stay selected.
Use liquid-tab-bar for switching between app sections rather than tools.

name: dot-grid
title: Dot grid
description: A dot field that bulges around the cursor like a lens and ripples from every click.
whenToUse: A landing page hero that should feel alive without video.
A background for an empty state, a sign in panel, or a launch countdown.
A playful section divider people can poke at.
whenNotToUse: Behind dense text or data; the moving dots compete with reading.
Use a static CSS dot pattern when no interaction is wanted.
Avoid stacking several on one screen; one reactive background is enough.

name: emoji-picker
title: Emoji picker
description: A full emoji picker with instant search, scroll-synced categories, skin tones, recently used emoji, and a virtualized, keyboard-navigable grid.
whenToUse: Message composers, comment boxes, and chat inputs.
Choosing an emoji for a status, a project, a page icon, or a label.
Any text field where people expect the full emoji set with search.
whenNotToUse: Use reactions for a small, fixed set of quick responses on a post or comment.
Use combobox or a select when the choices are a short, known list.
Do not use it as an icon picker; emoji render differently on every platform.

name: enrich-column
title: Enrich column
description: An AI enrichment column for a data table, where one prompt runs down every row and each cell shimmers while it works, then settles into a value with its source or a failure you can retry.
whenToUse: Enriching a list of companies or leads with facts an agent can look up (headcount, funding, tech stack).
Classifying or summarizing rows with one prompt, with a visible source per answer.
Showing per-row AI progress with stop, re-run and retry in a CRM, sales tool or internal admin.
whenNotToUse: Large spreadsheets with many columns and editing; use Data grid and add an AI column there.
A single question over a dataset; use Ask your data.
A log of one agent's tool calls; use Tool call.

name: funnel-chart
title: Funnel chart
description: A tapered conversion funnel with drop-off at every step, a device split that morphs the band, and dots that stream through it.
whenToUse: Conversion through a fixed sequence of steps.
Comparing how two segments convert through the same steps.
A hero chart on a growth or analytics page where the drop-off is the story.
whenNotToUse: Use sankey-flow when people can branch, skip, or loop between steps.
Use bar-chart for unordered categories.
Use line-chart for conversion over time.

name: generation-stats
title: Generation stats
description: A live stats strip for a streaming LLM response where time to first token, speed with a sparkline, output tokens and cost count up in tabular numerals beside the model's real mark, then settle and open into a latency and token cost breakdown.
whenToUse: Under assistant messages in a chat product that shows people what a response cost or how fast it was.
Playgrounds, eval runners and internal dev panels comparing models on latency, throughput and cost.
Admin or debugging views that inspect a single request's token usage and cache hit rate.
whenNotToUse: Use context-window to show how much of a model's context a conversation has used.
Use a chart or table for spend across many requests or days; this strip describes one response.
Use agent-status for a long running agent with steps; this measures one model call.

name: ghost-mascot
title: Ghost mascot
description: A floating ghost mascot whose soft sheet ripples at the hem while it hovers. It blinks when idle, turns toward you to listen, fades a little translucent while thinking, draws a tiny pen line while writing, smiles with a sparkle when done and wobbles once on an error.
whenToUse: Give an assistant a light, friendly face that shows what it is doing: in a reply header, in a composer, over an image canvas while it generates, or in an empty state.
Products that want generation to feel alive without a spinner, with states that still read at 24px.
whenNotToUse: Use agent-status when people need the steps, tools and elapsed time of a run, not just a mood.
Use text-shimmer alone for a plain "Thinking" line in dense interfaces where a character would distract.
Do not use it as a progress indicator with a known percentage; use a progress bar.

name: ghost-text
title: Ghost text
description: An inline AI autocomplete where muted ghost text continues your sentence exactly at the caret and Tab turns it solid in place. Cmd+Right takes it one word at a time, Escape fades it away, and a calm chip shows the model behind it.
whenToUse: Long-form fields people write in product: pull request descriptions, emails, support replies, issue bodies, release notes, CRM notes.
Short single-line fields where a likely completion saves typing, such as an email subject or a commit message.
Anywhere you want AI help that stays out of the way until the person pauses, and never changes their text without an explicit key press.
whenNotToUse: Use ai-composer for a chat-style prompt box that sends a message to an assistant.
Use code-suggestion for code diffs with accept and reject per hunk.
Use a combobox or command menu when the person picks from a list of known options rather than free text.
Avoid it in fields with sensitive content (passwords, card numbers, health data) unless your model provider and data policy allow it.

name: glass-card
title: Glass card
description: A glass info panel over a photo whose rim catches a pointer-following highlight while the card tilts; tap to morph it into a detail sheet.
whenToUse: Profile, host, or creator cards on a landing page or in a discovery grid.
A featured product or stay where the photo sells and the details can wait for a tap.
whenNotToUse: Dense grids of many cards; tilt and glass on every tile gets busy. Use card.
Cards that should open a full page; use card-to-article.

name: glass-menu
title: Glass menu
description: A glass action menu whose trigger morphs into the panel, with a highlight pill that glides between rows, one in-place submenu, and full keyboard support.
whenToUse: Actions for a photo, file, or card shown over an image or a colorful canvas.
A title menu in an editor or viewer, where the title itself opens the actions.
whenNotToUse: Plain settings pages with no imagery behind the menu. Use dropdown-menu on a neutral surface.
Navigation between pages. Use morph-nav or tabs.
Deep hierarchies. Use a command palette or a dedicated screen.

name: glass-segmented
title: Glass segmented
description: A glass segmented control whose liquid indicator stretches between segments and can be dragged and flung.
whenToUse: Switching the view of a photo, map, or media surface.
A compact filter over imagery, such as day, week, month on a hero chart.
whenNotToUse: Plain forms on neutral surfaces. Use segmented-control.
More than five options or long labels. Use tabs or a select.

name: glass-tabbar
title: Glass tab bar
description: A floating Liquid Glass tab bar that refracts what scrolls beneath it, with a glass lens that glides, magnifies and can be dragged between tabs, and an optional search bubble; it compacts on scroll down.
whenToUse: Mobile web apps and PWAs with three to five top level sections and one global action such as search.
Content feeds where the bar should step aside while reading and come back on scroll up.
whenNotToUse: Desktop layouts with many sections; use a sidebar or morph-nav.
Switching views inside a card; use segmented-control or tabs.

name: gravity-well
title: Gravity well
description: A grid of tiles that bends toward the cursor like spacetime, with a click that sends a shockwave through it.
whenToUse: A team, customer, or moodboard wall where playfulness is the point.
Landing page sections that show breadth: many logos, avatars, or photos at once.
whenNotToUse: Grids people must scan or click precisely, like file pickers; use a plain grid.
Large collections; use infinite-moodboard or photo-grid.

name: holo-card
title: Holo card
description: A member card that tilts toward you with a holographic foil and flips to its back.
whenToUse: A membership or subscription card on an account or welcome page.
A shareable profile, badge, or achievement that people will screenshot.
A collectible or reward reveal.
whenNotToUse: Use card for ordinary content; the effect is too loud for lists.
Use depth-cards when several items need a subtle parallax.
Avoid it for text people need to read carefully; the sheen moves over the content.

name: image-generation
title: Image generation
description: An image studio where each image forms on a dot matrix: a soft halftone wave breathes across the grid, the dots take the colours of the coming photo and grow into a coloured halftone, then blur away into the sharp photo. One large canvas with a mono size label, a filmstrip of four variations, a prompt bar with model and ratio, and upscale with a sweeping dot band, vary or download, with real provider marks and a built-in simulation.
whenToUse: A text to image feature inside a product: marketing asset tools, listing photo helpers, slide or doc illustration.
Any flow where people compare a few candidates and continue with one (upscale, vary, download).
Prototyping an image model integration before the backend exists, using the built in simulation.
whenNotToUse: A full canvas editor with layers, masks and inpainting; build on a canvas library instead.
Drawing a sketch to turn into an image; use sketch-to-image.
Showing a single image with a loading state and no generation controls; use blur-image.

name: image-reveal
title: Image reveal
description: An image generation canvas where a soft, blurred preview made from the image's own colors sharpens top to bottom behind a soft-edged band. It works the way ChatGPT, Midjourney and Gemini show images forming, with fine film grain, a translucent progress pill and calm queued and error states.
whenToUse: Showing an image model's progress on a canvas or in a chat reply.
A batch of image variations sampling side by side.
A queued image job that should feel alive before it starts.
whenNotToUse: Plain image loading from a CDN; use a blur-up placeholder or a skeleton.
Text generation or tool calls; use text-shimmer or tool-call.
Determinate file uploads; use progress.

name: image-trail
title: Image trail
description: Moving the pointer leaves a curated trail of photos that pop in, lean, and fade away.
whenToUse: A portfolio or agency hero that should feel alive on first move.
Travel, food, or product stories told through a sequence of photos.
Launch pages that want an instantly playful surface.
whenNotToUse: Use photo-grid or lightbox-gallery when people need to look at each photo.
Use hover-image-list to preview one image per row in a list.
Avoid it behind long text that people need to read.

name: ink-fluid
title: Ink fluid
description: A real time fluid simulation behind your hero: the cursor stirs soft ink that swirls, settles and fades; calm when left alone.
whenToUse: A landing hero or sign in screen that should feel alive without a video.
Empty states and waiting screens where a gentle, interactive background rewards curiosity.
whenNotToUse: Dense product surfaces such as tables and forms. Movement behind data distracts.
More than one per page; each instance runs its own simulation.

name: install-snippet
title: Install snippet
description: A "get started in 30 seconds" card where framework tabs, three numbered steps and highlighted snippets take a developer from install to first event. Generate key wipes a fresh API key into the placeholder in place.
whenToUse: A quickstart that has to work for several frameworks without three pages of docs.
Onboarding where creating an API key is part of getting started.
Marketing pages for developer tools that want to show how little setup it takes.
whenNotToUse: A single code sample with no steps: use code-block.
Trying requests against a live API: use api-playground.
Long setup guides with many branches: write docs pages and link to them.

name: keycap-keyboard
title: Keycap keyboard
description: Mechanical keycaps that sink and light up as you type, with the text above the board.
whenToUse: Landing pages for keyboard-first products and developer tools.
Onboarding that teaches shortcuts by lighting the keys they use.
Playful empty states and easter eggs.
whenNotToUse: Form input; use a real text field.
On-screen keyboards for accessibility needs; use the platform's.

name: lightbox-gallery
title: Lightbox gallery
description: A masonry grid where photos zoom from their slot into a viewer you can swipe, pinch, and drag away.
whenToUse: Photo collections people browse and inspect up close, such as trips, portfolios, or listings.
Mixed portrait and landscape sets that should keep their aspect ratios in a masonry grid.
whenNotToUse: Use photo-grid for a square grid with pinch zoom between densities.
Use carousel for a single inline row without a viewer.
Use dialog to show one arbitrary piece of content.

name: link-unfurl
title: Link unfurl
description: A composer where pasting a URL shows a loading shimmer on the link, then unfurls it into a rich preview card with title, image and favicon in one morph, which can be collapsed back to the inline link or removed.
whenToUse: A message or comment composer where pasted links should show what they point to before sending.
Product marketing that shows how a chat or notes app handles links.
whenNotToUse: Use hover-card to preview a link someone reads, not writes.
Use mention-input when the tokens are people or records rather than web links, and rich-text-editor for long formatted documents.

name: liquid-tab-bar
title: Liquid tab bar
description: Tabs with a lens selection that slides between them, swaps labels cleanly, and fills in icons as it passes.
whenToUse: Switching between a handful of peer sections with icons, such as an app's main areas.
Bottom or top bars on mobile-style layouts where the selection should feel physical.
Tabs that carry badge counts for new items.
whenNotToUse: Use tabs for text-only panels inside a page.
Use segmented-control for compact filters or view toggles.
Use morph-nav for site navigation with dropdown panels.

name: live-visitors
title: Live visitors
description: A realtime visitors card where the live count rolls digit by digit, new arrivals ping in on a dotted world map, the top pages reorder with bars, and signups and upgrades tick in with country flags.
whenToUse: Realtime visitors on a marketing site or app, next to signups and upgrades as they happen.
Launch days and campaigns where a team watches traffic and conversions live.
Admin and growth dashboards that need one glanceable tile for right now.
whenNotToUse: Historical trends over days or weeks; use a chart with axes.
Precise geography or per-country breakdowns; use a table or a proper map.
A single number with no context; use a stat card.

name: llm-cost-calculator
title: LLM cost calculator
description: A pricing calculator for LLM workloads. Set tokens per request, requests per day and prompt caching, and eight current models re-rank by monthly cost. Bars glide and prices roll as you drag.
whenToUse: A pricing or settings page needs an honest monthly estimate for an LLM workload across several models.
People pick a model for a feature and should see how cost moves with prompt size, output length, traffic and caching.
An internal tool compares provider prices before a migration or a budget review.
whenNotToUse: Use model-picker to choose a model in a chat or composer without a cost comparison.
Use context-window to show the live token usage of one conversation against a model's context window.
Use usage-meter or usage-pricing for actual metered spend against a plan; this estimates, it does not report.

name: meeting-summary
title: Meeting summary
description: An AI meeting notes card: the header shows the Google Meet or Zoom mark, the attendees and the duration. Summary, Decisions and Action items stream in after a short summarizing pass. Hover any line to see the transcript quote it came from, then check off action items or send them to Linear or Notion.
whenToUse: Showing AI notes after a call in a CRM, a recruiting tool, a meeting recorder or a team workspace.
Turning a transcript into decisions and owned tasks that people can push to their tracker.
Any summary where readers should be able to check a point against what was actually said.
whenNotToUse: Live captions or a running transcript during the call; use text-stream or a transcript view.
A general task list with no meeting behind it; use checkbox rows in your own list.
Long documents with many sections; render them as a document page instead of a card.

name: mega-menu-morph
title: Mega menu morph
description: A site header whose menus share one floating panel. Moving between sections morphs its size, slides the next menu in from that side and glides the caret under the new trigger, with hover intent, a safe triangle and an accordion sheet on narrow screens.
whenToUse: A marketing site header with product, solution, developer and company sections that each need a rich menu.
A documentation or platform site whose top sections deserve descriptions, a featured story or a status line.
Anywhere visitors browse several menus in a row and repeated open and close animations would feel busy.
whenNotToUse: Use morph-nav for a compact floating pill navigation with search built in.
Use dropdown-menu for a single list of actions or links behind one button.
Use tabs or a docs-sidebar style navigation for moving between views inside a product.

name: metric-ticker
title: Metric ticker
description: A strip of live KPIs that roll to new values digit by digit and flash their change; rest on one to pause the strip and open its recent trend as a sparkline.
whenToUse: A compact live readout of several KPIs above a dashboard, a status page or a trading view.
Wall screens and operations views where values change on their own and people glance at them.
A header strip that must fit anywhere from a phone to a wide monitor without redesign.
whenNotToUse: Use metric-card or stat-card for one or two headline numbers with room for context.
Use line-chart or sparkline when the trend over time is the main content, not a detail.
Avoid it for values that change once a day; the live treatment would promise more than it delivers.

name: mixture-of-experts
title: Mixture of experts
description: An illustration of mixture of experts routing: each token is scored by a router, travels to its top experts, and their outputs merge into the token's result.
whenToUse: Explaining why a mixture of experts model is cheap per token: only the chosen experts run, which the active parameter readout makes concrete.
Showing how a gate scores experts, picks the top k and blends their outputs, with real or sample scores.
Teaching load balancing and expert capacity, where an uneven router overloads some experts and drops tokens.
whenNotToUse: Use model-router to pick which model handles a request in a product; this card explains routing inside one model.
Use attention-map to show which tokens a token attends to, rather than which experts process it.
Use token-inspector to show tokenization, token ids and probabilities of generated text.
Use speculative-decoding to explain draft and verify generation speedups.

name: model-card
title: Model card
description: A model details card where switching models rolls every price, limit and score in place, a token slider estimates monthly cost live, and benchmark bars show each model's rank on hover. Compare crossfades to a side-by-side table against any rival with the better values marked, and the card never changes size.
whenToUse: The detail pane of a model picker, showing what the highlighted model can do and what it costs before someone selects it.
Model pages in docs or a marketplace, with limits, prices and a quick benchmark read against close rivals.
Settings where a team picks a default model and wants a side by side check against an alternative.
whenNotToUse: Use model-picker to choose between many models; pair it with this card for the details.
Use context-window to show how full a live conversation's context is.
Use a pricing table for plan pricing; this card shows per token API prices.
Do not use it for official benchmark leaderboards with many models; the bar list shows three models.

name: model-training
title: Model training
description: Training data batches feed a small neural net diagram whose connections strengthen, a loss curve descends beside it, and an evaluation check turns green at the end.
whenToUse: An AI or ML product section that explains training, fine-tuning or evaluation in one glance.
Docs pages introducing batches, epochs, loss curves or held-out evaluation.
whenNotToUse: Use line-chart or metric-card for real, live training metrics.
Use data-flow to explain how records move through a pipeline, and pipeline-status for real job status.

name: morph-loader
title: Morph loader
description: Tiny loaders that morph between shapes and fold into a check or a cross when done.
whenToUse: Inline progress inside a button, row, or field where the result should appear in the same spot.
Short operations that end in a clear success or failure, such as save, publish, or upload.
Any spinner where a tiny, crisp, brand-consistent mark matters.
whenNotToUse: Use progress when the percentage is known.
Use skeleton when content is loading into a layout.
Use action-button when the whole button should morph its label too.

name: morph-nav
title: Morph nav
description: A navigation bar that morphs into rich menus, search, and a compact state as one surface.
whenToUse: The top navigation of a marketing or product site with a few sections that each hold several destinations.
Headers where search should grow out of the bar instead of opening a separate modal.
Sites that want one primary action, such as Sign up, pinned to the end of the bar.
whenNotToUse: Use liquid-tab-bar for an app-style switcher between a handful of peer sections.
Use tabs for switching views inside a page.
Use dropdown-menu when you only need one menu of commands, not site navigation.

name: multi-region-failover
title: Multi-region failover
description: Animated multi-region failover on a 2.5D stage: users stream requests through a global load balancer to two regions; the primary degrades, fails three health checks, traffic shifts smoothly to the healthy region, then it recovers, passes three checks and traffic ramps back to an even split.
whenToUse: A reliability, infrastructure or pricing page that needs to show why running in two regions keeps a service up during an outage.
Docs for health checks, failover policies, traffic weights or slow start, where viewers should step through detection, failover, recovery and rebalance.
Incident write-ups and postmortems that explain how traffic moved during a regional outage.
whenNotToUse: Use database-replication to show a primary database failing over to a replica.
Use circuit-breaker for one service failing fast against a failing dependency.
Use autoscale for instances added and removed with load in one place.
Use a real status or monitoring component to report actual region health.

name: now-playing
title: Now playing
description: Grow a mini player into the full player in one continuous morph.
whenToUse: Media that keeps playing while people browse, such as music, podcasts, or audio lessons.
A mini player bar that expands into a full player with artwork and a scrubber.
whenNotToUse: Use bottom-sheet or dialog for a one-off overlay that is not a player.
Use voice-recorder for recording and playing back short voice notes.
Use slider for a plain seek bar without the player chrome.

name: orbit-logos
title: Orbit logos
description: An integrations showcase with brand logos orbiting your product mark on tilted rings. Hover or focus one to rest the orbit, draw a connection, and see what it does.
whenToUse: An integrations or ecosystem hero on a marketing site.
An integrations settings screen where people browse, read about, and connect tools.
A launch page showing everything a product plugs into.
whenNotToUse: Use a logo marquee for a long list of customer logos.
Use a searchable grid or table for catalogs larger than about twenty integrations.

name: orbit-menu
title: Orbit menu
description: Hold a button and its actions orbit out, ready to pick with a drag.
whenToUse: Three to six quick actions on one object, such as a note or photo.
Touch-first surfaces where press, drag, and release should fire an action in one gesture.
whenNotToUse: Use dropdown-menu or context-menu for longer or text-heavy lists.
Use dock for tools that stay selected.
Use action-button for a single action.

name: page-curl
title: Page curl
description: A small magazine you read by dragging page corners, with a real fold, lit curl, and flick to turn.
whenToUse: Editorial and brand showcases where paper is part of the story.
Menus, catalogs, and yearbooks with a handful of spreads.
whenNotToUse: Use carousel or a scrolling page for long content or content people search.
Use a document viewer for dense text that needs zoom and selection.

name: payment-flow
title: Payment flow
description: A card tap goes to a processor, then the network, then the bank and back with authorization, then settlement; each hop lights up with a status label and the amount travels as a chip.
whenToUse: A payments or checkout landing section that explains authorization and settlement.
Docs pages introducing processors, card networks, issuers, fees, and payout timing.
whenNotToUse: Use checkout-flow or checkout-live for a real checkout form.
Use webhook-fanout to explain what happens after a payment event is emitted.

name: photo-grid
title: Photo grid
description: Pinch through zoom levels and open any photo straight from its cell.
whenToUse: A browsable photo library or album where people zoom between column counts.
Galleries that need favorites and a full-screen viewer with a filmstrip.
Touch and trackpad users who expect pinch to change density.
whenNotToUse: Use lightbox-gallery for a masonry layout that keeps each photo's aspect ratio.
Use carousel for a short inline slideshow.
Use image-compare for before and after pairs.

name: pii-redaction
title: PII redaction
description: A guardrail card where personal data is redacted before the prompt reaches the model. Scan marks each name, email, phone number and card with its type and swaps it for a placeholder like [EMAIL_1]. The safe prompt travels to Claude, and the reply comes back with the original values put back for the person.
whenToUse: Explaining or proving a privacy guardrail in an AI product: support assistants, health or finance copilots, enterprise chat.
A settings or onboarding screen where admins see what the PII filter does before they turn it on.
A playground where people paste text and see exactly what would reach the model.
whenNotToUse: Use ai-chat or ai-composer for the conversation itself; redact behind the scenes and show this card only where the guardrail needs explaining.
Do not rely on the built-in detector for compliance; pass a real DLP service through detect.
Use tool-call to show an arbitrary tool step in a transcript.

name: pixel-mascot
title: Pixel mascot
description: A pixel-art robot that shows what an AI assistant is doing. It idles, thinks, types, celebrates and errors in frame-stepped sprite animations, and stays crisp at every integer size from 24px to 192px.
whenToUse: A friendly generating indicator next to an assistant reply or in a chat composer.
An empty state or onboarding panel where a small character makes an AI feature feel approachable.
Image or canvas generation, where a mascot in the corner shows thinking, drawing and done.
Products with a playful or retro visual voice that still want precise, calm motion.
whenNotToUse: Detailed agent progress with steps and timings; use agent-status or agent-timeline.
Dense tables or toolbars where a 24px character is noise; use status-dot or a spinner.
Serious or regulated contexts (finance, health, legal) where a character feels flippant; use text-shimmer.
Showing model reasoning content; use reasoning-block.

name: presence-stack
title: Presence stack
description: Avatars of the people here now: joins pop in as the stack reflows, a counter rolls past the limit, dots show typing and idle, and hover fans it out with a gliding name label.
whenToUse: A document, board or design file header that shows who is here right now.
A call or meeting roster where people come and go and some are talking or idle.
Any realtime surface where joins, leaves and typing should be felt, not just counted.
whenNotToUse: Use avatar-group for a static list of owners, assignees or members that does not change while you look at it.
Use live-cursors when you also need cursors and selections on a canvas; it includes its own small stack.
Use a plain count for very large rooms, such as a livestream with thousands of viewers.

name: prize-wheel
title: Prize wheel
description: A referral or promo prize wheel you flick to spin, with real angular momentum, a flexible pointer that ticks against each peg, weighted segments set by the host, a slow suspenseful settle, and the won segment lifting into a reward card with a copyable code.
whenToUse: A referral or launch page that rewards a signup with a discount code.
An in-product moment that grants one of several perks, such as a milestone reward.
whenNotToUse: Use a plain coupon card or copy button when everyone gets the same reward.
Avoid it in serious flows such as billing or checkout, where chance feels out of place.

name: product-gallery
title: Product gallery
description: A product gallery with a hover magnifier, gliding thumbnails, and color and size variants that crossfade photos.
whenToUse: Product detail pages with several photos per color and a size picker.
Stores where shoppers need to zoom into fabric, texture, or small print.
Variants that sell out per color and should be struck through, not hidden.
whenNotToUse: Use lightbox-gallery for a photo grid that opens into a viewer, with no variants.
Use carousel for marketing slides or cards.
Use photo-grid for a masonry of images without a main photo.

name: prompt-cache
title: Prompt cache
description: An animated explainer for prompt caching: the shared prefix of each request is cached once, later requests read it back, and the cost and time saved add up.
whenToUse: A docs page or blog post that explains why a stable prefix makes repeat requests cheaper and faster.
A pricing or usage page that shows how cache reads, writes and the time to live affect cost.
Developer onboarding for an AI product where prompt order and cache breakpoints matter.
whenNotToUse: Use context-window to show how much of a model's window a conversation fills and when it compacts.
Use token-inspector to show how text splits into tokens and what each costs.
Use model-picker or model-router when the subject is choosing a model rather than reusing a prompt.
Use a real chart of cache hit rate over time for production analytics; this is a teaching illustration with a simulated clock.

name: provider-keys
title: Provider keys
description: A settings card for bring-your-own-key AI products. Each provider row shows its real mark, the masked key, a status and when the key was last used. You can reveal a key for five seconds, copy, rotate or remove it with undo. Adding or rotating a key opens an inline form that checks the format as you type, then tests the connection before saving.
whenToUse: A settings page where users add their own Anthropic, OpenAI, Google AI, Mistral or xAI keys.
Showing which providers are connected, which keys were rejected, and when each key was last used.
Letting users rotate a leaked key or remove one with a short undo window.
whenNotToUse: Choosing a model for a request; use model-picker.
Managing your own product's API keys for customers with scopes and expiry; use secret-rotation or a table.
Showing spend or rate limits; use usage-meter.

name: provider-status
title: Provider status
description: A status card for the AI providers your product depends on. Each row shows the provider's real mark, its health as an icon and label, p50 latency and a 30-day uptime bar with a tooltip for each day. An incident row expands into its timeline of updates, and the card checks again on a visible countdown.
whenToUse: Showing the live health, latency and recent uptime of the model providers your product routes to.
Explaining degraded AI features to users or admins with the provider's incident updates in place.
A routing or fallback settings page where people need to see which providers are healthy right now.
whenNotToUse: A full public status page with components, subscriptions and history: build a page, not a card.
A single provider's state inside a chat header: use agent-status or a small badge.
Detailed latency charts over time: use a chart component.
exports: AnthropicMark, OpenaiMark, GeminiColorMark, MistralColorMark, XaiMark, AwsMark

name: race-bar-chart
title: Race bar chart
description: A ranking over time: bars overtake each other on springs, values count up, and a timeline you can play or scrub.
whenToUse: Showing how the leaders of a ranking change across many periods.
A launch or recap moment where the motion itself is the point.
Letting people scrub to any period and read exact values.
whenNotToUse: Use line-chart when exact trends over time matter more than rank.
Use bar-chart for a single period's comparison.
Avoid for dashboards people glance at; autoplay competes with other content.

name: radar-chart
title: Radar chart
description: Two or three profiles on one web: shapes morph when you swap a profile, and a sweep across the axes compares values in place.
whenToUse: Comparing the profile of a few options across shared measures.
Showing strengths and gaps at a glance, such as scores or ratings.
whenNotToUse: Use bar-chart when the precise difference on one measure matters.
Use plan-matrix for feature comparisons with yes or no values.
Avoid more than three profiles; the shapes stop being readable.

name: realtime-stream
title: Realtime stream
description: A live line that scrolls at 60fps as readings arrive, holds still on hover to read, and pops a marker on every anomaly.
whenToUse: Live monitoring panels and status pages.
A hero on an infrastructure or observability page where motion shows the system is alive.
whenNotToUse: Use line-chart for static time series.
Use brush-chart for long histories people zoom into.
Use sparkline for a tiny trend inside a stat.

name: reasoning-block
title: Reasoning block
description: The collapsible thinking block of an AI reply. While the model thinks, a shimmering label counts the seconds and the latest reasoning streams underneath. When it finishes, it folds to "Thought for 7s" and opens to show the full reasoning as calm steps with headings.
whenToUse: Showing a reasoning model's thinking above its answer in a chat or agent transcript.
Letting people audit why an assistant reached a recommendation without crowding the reply.
Restoring past messages where the reasoning should stay folded with its original thinking time.
whenNotToUse: Tool or function calls with inputs and outputs: use ToolCall.
A multi step agent plan with checkable tasks: use Agent plan.
A one line busy indicator with no reasoning to show: use TextShimmer on its own.

name: reasoning-tree
title: Reasoning tree
description: An illustration of tree search over thoughts: candidates are scored, weak branches fade, the best expand, and the winning path from question to answer draws in.
whenToUse: Explainers, docs and landing pages that teach tree of thoughts, beam search or test time search over reasoning steps.
Showing why a wider search can beat a greedy one, with a control the reader can change and replay.
A visual summary of how an agent weighed options before it chose a plan.
whenNotToUse: Use agent-run or research-run to show a real agent's steps and output as they stream.
Use agent-loop to explain the plan, act and observe cycle of a tool using agent.
Use speculative-decoding or attention-map for token level mechanics rather than whole thoughts.
Use model-router when the decision is which model handles a request.

name: referral-card
title: Referral card
description: A give-and-get referral card where people copy or share their invite link, invite friends by email as chips, and watch invites move from invited to signed up to earned, with the credit total counting up and a milestone reward unlocking.
whenToUse: A referral or invite program in account settings, billing or an onboarding checklist.
Showing a person what their invites have earned and how close they are to a bonus reward.
whenNotToUse: Team member invites with roles and permissions; use a members table.
Public leaderboards or affiliate payouts with many columns; use a table.

name: reply-draft
title: Reply draft
description: An AI email reply drafter where Claude streams a reply under a received Gmail message. Quick replies steer a fresh draft, tone and length rewrite it with a single crossfade, and you can edit the finished draft before you insert it.
whenToUse: Drafting a reply to an email, ticket or message with an AI model, where the reader reviews and edits before sending.
Offering quick reply intents plus tone and length controls for generated text.
Showing an AI writing feature on a landing page with a realistic, self-playing example.
whenNotToUse: Free-form chat with a model: use a chat or composer component instead.
Inline autocomplete while typing: use ghost-text.
Sending the email itself: this component inserts a draft; your composer owns sending.

name: response-feedback
title: Response feedback
description: A feedback control for AI replies where thumbs down opens an inline panel with reason chips and an optional note, thumbs up fills and asks what was good, and a submit shows a short thank-you before folding back into the row.
whenToUse: Collecting thumbs up and down on AI replies in a chat, copilot or search answer.
Gathering structured reasons (inaccurate, unsafe) for model evaluation or support triage.
Adding a message action row with copy and regenerate next to feedback.
whenNotToUse: Star or numeric ratings of a product or session: use rating.
General product feedback not tied to one reply: use feedback-morph.
Long surveys with many questions: use a form or dialog.

name: sand-text
title: Sand text
description: A headline made of sand that pours into the letters, crumbles where the cursor digs, and heals itself.
whenToUse: A hero headline or section title that should be fun to touch.
Short words that change on a selection, like a product name or theme.
whenNotToUse: Body copy or long headings; use in-view-title or text-reveal.
Text that must stay readable while people interact near it, like form labels.

name: sankey-flow
title: Sankey flow
description: Flows between stages as ribbons with drifting particles; hover any node or ribbon to pour its share through the whole journey.
whenToUse: Showing how a total splits and recombines across three to five stages.
Explaining where a funnel leaks, with the share at each step one hover away.
Comparing two periods of the same flow by switching data.
whenNotToUse: Use bar-chart for a simple linear funnel with no branches.
Use sunburst for a strict hierarchy where each part has one parent.
Avoid more than about 12 nodes per column; small flows become unreadable slivers.

name: share-access
title: Share access
description: A share panel: invite people as validated email chips with suggestions, change roles from a compact menu, remove with undo, switch link access and copy the link, with every change landing in place.
whenToUse: A Share button on a document, board or project that controls who can open it and what they can do.
Inviting teammates by email with suggestions from a workspace directory.
Managing link sharing next to per person access in one place.
whenNotToUse: Use the invite-people block for inviting people to a whole workspace with seats and plans.
Use copy-button alone when there is only a public link to share.
Use a full settings page with a data table for organisations with hundreds of members and groups.

name: share-sheet
title: Share sheet
description: A Share button that opens into a panel with copy link, access level, channels, and people to send to.
whenToUse: A Share button on a document, design, or board header where people share often.
Sharing flows that combine copy link, access level, and sending to a few recent people.
Posting to a small set of channels, such as Slack or email, with in-place pending and done feedback.
whenNotToUse: Use copy-button when all you need is to copy a URL.
Use dialog when sharing needs a full form, such as roles per person or an email search.
Use popover for a small menu of share targets with no people picker.

name: sheet-stack
title: Sheet stack
description: Nested sheets that stack with depth, drag to dismiss, and become stacked dialogs on wide screens.
whenToUse: Mobile settings where each row opens a deeper page and back should feel spatial.
Nested pickers, such as choosing a workspace and then a project inside it.
Flows that should be a bottom sheet on phones and a centered dialog on desktop from one declaration.
whenNotToUse: Use dialog for a single confirmation or form with no nested steps.
Use bottom-sheet for one sheet with snap points.
Use multi-step-form when steps are sequential rather than drill-down.

name: skeleton-morph
title: Skeleton morph
description: Loading skeletons that grow into the real content, block by block, instead of swapping.
whenToUse: Profile cards, feeds, and lists that load in under a few seconds.
Dashboards where the layout is known before the data arrives.
Places where a hard swap from gray boxes to content would feel jarring.
whenNotToUse: Use skeleton for long lists of hundreds of rows; layout animation there is costly.
Use a progress indicator when loading takes more than a few seconds.
Avoid it when the loaded layout is unknown in advance.

name: smart-form-fill
title: Smart form fill
description: A paste-to-fill form card where AI reads an email signature or messy notes and fills a contact field by field. Each value flashes in with a confidence dot, its source lights up in the pasted text, low-confidence guesses ask for review, and Undo puts the old values back.
whenToUse: People paste an email signature, a forwarded message or notes and expect the record to fill itself.
You need visible confidence and an easy review path before AI-filled data is saved.
Onboarding or CRM flows where typing six fields by hand is the main friction.
whenNotToUse: Plain data entry with no unstructured source; use form-field and input.
Long multi-page applications; use multi-step-form and add a paste step to one page.
Bulk imports of many records; use a table import flow instead of one card.

name: social-proof-toast
title: Social proof toast
description: A stack of social proof notifications for landing and pricing pages, where recent trials, upgrades and verified purchases from people and companies arrive every few seconds. The stack pauses and fans out on hover, and visitors can dismiss any toast.
whenToUse: Showing recent trials, purchases or upgrades on a landing or pricing page.
A live activity feed for a launch or waitlist page (people joining, teams upgrading).
Highlighting verified purchases from known companies near a checkout CTA.
whenNotToUse: System feedback after a user action (saved, copied, failed): use toast or undo-toast.
Inside a signed in product where activity is not marketing: use an activity feed list.
When you do not have real events to show; fabricated social proof erodes trust.

name: source-cards
title: Source cards
description: A row of cited sources under an AI answer where cards stream in with real site marks while the model searches, the overflow collapses into a stack of favicons, hovering lifts a preview with the passage, and an inline [n] citation highlights its card.
whenToUse: Citations under an AI search or docs assistant answer.
Showing live search progress ("Searching 3 of 8") while an agent browses.
Linking inline [n] references in generated text to the pages they came from.
whenNotToUse: A full search results page with many results and filters; use a list layout instead.
Tool calls with arguments and outputs; use tool-call.
A single link preview inside prose; use a tooltip or hover card.

name: speculative-decoding
title: Speculative decoding
description: An illustration of speculative decoding: a fast draft model guesses a few tokens, the target model checks them in one pass, and accepted guesses join the answer.
whenToUse: Explaining why a product answers faster: docs, model pages, inference dashboards and blog posts about latency.
Showing a recorded speculative run from your own server, with acceptance and tokens per pass for a chosen draft length.
Teaching the trade off between draft length, acceptance rate and speedup with a slider people can try.
whenNotToUse: Use text-stream to show an answer streaming to a user; this card explains the mechanism behind the speed.
Use token-inspector to look at token probabilities and alternatives for one answer.
Use model-router to explain how requests are sent to different models; speculative decoding runs two models on every request.
Use attention-map or mixture-of-experts for what happens inside a single forward pass.

name: speech-player
title: Speech player
description: A read-aloud player for AI replies. The Read aloud button in the message's action row turns into a compact player with play, a scrubbable progress bar, speed and a voice picker, and a highlight follows the spoken word through the reply, karaoke style.
whenToUse: A chat or answer surface where people want a reply read out, with the spoken word followed in the text.
Accessibility and hands free reading for long AI answers, summaries or briefings.
Previewing TTS voices and speeds against real product copy.
whenNotToUse: Use dictation-button to turn speech into text in a composer.
Use a plain audio player for podcasts or long recordings without a transcript to highlight.

name: split-bar
title: Split bar
description: A single 100% bar split into shares: rest on a segment to widen it and read its exact figures, toggle segments from the legend and the rest reflow, with labels inside when they fit and on leader lines when they don't.
whenToUse: A compact part to whole view that fits in a card row or a dashboard header.
Comparing shares where people also want exact figures on demand and the option to leave a category out.
Showing how a mix changes between periods or filters with one continuous reflow.
whenNotToUse: Use bar-chart to compare absolute values across many categories.
Use donut-chart when the total in the middle is the headline, or waffle-chart for a count of units.
Use a stacked chart over time when the trend of each share matters more than today's split.

name: starter-prompts
title: Starter prompts
description: A greeting and a grid of starter cards for the empty state of an AI app. The cards are grouped into Write, Code, Analyze and Plan tabs, and a shuffle swaps them with a short staggered crossfade. Picking a card fills the composer, and cards that use a connected app show its mark (Gmail, GitHub, Notion, Linear, Google Calendar).
whenToUse: The empty state of a chat, copilot or agent, before the first message.
Teaching what an assistant can do with connected tools, such as Gmail, GitHub or Notion.
Onboarding a new workspace with a few tailored, ready to send prompts.
whenNotToUse: Inside a running conversation; use follow-up suggestion chips in the chat thread instead.
A command launcher with search; use command-palette or ai-command.
A single inline suggestion in a text field; use ghost-text.

name: sticker-peel
title: Sticker peel
description: Peel stickers off a surface with a real curl, move them around, and stick them back down.
whenToUse: A personal or team page where people arrange badges, achievements, or brand stickers.
A launch or marketing moment that invites people to play with the product's marks.
A reward screen where earned stickers are placed on a surface.
whenNotToUse: Use reorderable-list or a sortable grid when the order of items carries meaning.
Use note-stack for content people need to read and rearrange.
Avoid it on dense work screens; it is a delight surface, not an input.

name: stretch-refresh
title: Stretch refresh
description: Pull a feed down and a line stretches to tell you when to let go.
whenToUse: Timelines, inboxes, and activity feeds where new entries arrive at the top.
Panels that should support pull to refresh by touch, mouse drag, and trackpad scroll.
whenNotToUse: Use a plain list for static content that never refreshes.
Use pagination for paging through older items.
Use timeline for a static history of events.

name: sunburst
title: Sunburst
description: A hierarchy in rings: click a segment and every arc swings around it as the new centre, with a breadcrumb back and a rolling total.
whenToUse: Drilling into where a total comes from, one level at a time.
Showing the share of each part within its parent and within the whole.
Dashboards where a compact, explorable overview beats a long table.
whenNotToUse: Use donut-chart for a single level of parts.
Use tree-table when people need to compare exact values across many rows.
Avoid it for more than about 150 leaves; thin slivers stop being readable.

name: team-switcher
title: Team switcher
description: A workspace switcher like Linear, Vercel or Slack. The trigger shows the current workspace's logo and plan. The menu has search, your role in each workspace and a Cmd+1 to 9 shortcut for each, and lets you create or join a workspace inline. A highlight glides between rows, and switching crossfades the trigger through a short loading state.
whenToUse: Switching between organizations, teams or workspaces in a multi-tenant SaaS app.
An account or project picker that needs search, roles and keyboard shortcuts.
Letting people create a new workspace or accept an invite without leaving the current page.
whenNotToUse: Picking from a short static list of options in a form: use a select or segmented control.
Global navigation across pages and commands: use the command palette block.
Switching between two or three views of the same data: use tabs.

name: ticket-router
title: Ticket router
description: A support ticket router where messages from Gmail, Intercom, Slack and Zendesk come in one at a time. An AI classifier labels each one with intent, sentiment and confidence, and the ticket moves into a team lane with an assignee. Low confidence tickets wait in a review lane, and one click there routes them to the suggested team.
whenToUse: Showing how an AI classifier triages inbound support messages into team queues.
A live triage widget in a helpdesk or ops dashboard, with a human review lane for low confidence.
Landing page or onboarding demos of AI routing for support products.
whenNotToUse: A full ticket inbox with search and bulk actions; use a table or list layout.
A single tool step in a chat transcript; use tool-call.
Generic multi step agent progress; use agent-status or agent-plan.

name: time-dial
title: Time dial
description: Spin a dial to pick an hour and see which team cities are at work.
whenToUse: Planning a moment across two to five cities, such as calls, releases, or handovers.
Distributed teams that need to see at a glance who is inside working hours.
whenNotToUse: Use time-picker for a single local time.
Use date-picker or calendar when the day matters more than the hour.
Use slider for a plain numeric range.

name: tldr-toggle
title: TL;DR toggle
description: An article card with a Full, Summary and Key points switch and a length slider. Switching streams an AI summary in place of the article as the card's height springs to fit, and each key point links back to the paragraph it came from, which gets scrolled to and highlighted.
whenToUse: Offering a quick summary or key points above or in place of a long article, doc or report.
Letting readers verify AI claims against the source, through key points that link back to paragraphs.
Reading surfaces where people choose how much detail they want with a length control.
whenNotToUse: Open-ended questions about content: use an answer or chat component such as ai-answer.
Short content under a couple of paragraphs, where a summary saves no time.
Summaries of many documents at once: use a list or a digest layout instead of one card per item.

name: toc-progress
title: Table of contents progress
description: A table of contents that reads along with you: a line bends through the nested headings, fills as you scroll, and carries a marker to the current section, with smooth jumps and a time-left countdown.
whenToUse: A documentation page, guide or blog post long enough that readers jump between sections.
An engineering write up or policy where knowing how much is left helps readers commit to it.
Any long article in its own scroll container, such as a help panel or a reader view.
whenNotToUse: Use tabs when sections are alternatives rather than parts of one document.
Use scroll-progress-ring for a compact overall progress indicator without navigation.
Skip it for pages with fewer than four headings; a plain list of anchors is enough.

name: tone-tuner
title: Tone tuner
description: A brand voice card where two sliders (formality and detail) and Friendly, Confident and Empathetic chips rewrite a customer reply. Each changed sentence crossfades in place, new words can be highlighted against the original, and Copy takes the current version.
whenToUse: A composer or help desk reply that offers AI tone controls before sending.
Brand voice tooling where marketers compare versions of the same copy.
Any rewrite where people want to steer with a few dials rather than write a prompt.
whenNotToUse: Free form AI editing with a prompt box: use a chat or composer instead.
Long documents: the card is sized for a message of a few paragraphs.
Exact line by line code or contract diffs: use a dedicated diff view.

name: tool-call
title: Tool call
description: A tool call row for agent transcripts: the tool's mark and the call in plain words, a live state while it runs, and the input and output a click away, with approval and retry when needed.
whenToUse: Showing what tools an AI agent used inside a chat or agent transcript, with the arguments and results one click away.
Human in the loop actions where a call must be allowed or denied inline before it runs, such as posting a message or writing to a database.
Making failures recoverable in place: a timed out query with its reason and a Retry button.
Debug and audit views where developers need to copy exact tool inputs and outputs.
whenNotToUse: Use agent-run for a full multi step run with a plan, a timeline and live logs rather than inline rows in a message.
Use agent-approvals for a queue of pending approvals across many agents and runs.
Use research-run when the work is mostly web research with sources and a streamed report.
Use mcp-servers to manage which tools an agent can reach, not to show individual calls.

name: training-run
title: Training run
description: A fine-tuning job card where a live train and validation loss curve draws across a fixed step axis that doubles as the epoch progress bar. It shows the learning rate, elapsed time, ETA and the latest evals and checkpoints, has Pause and Cancel while it runs, and ends in results with a Deploy button.
whenToUse: A fine-tuning or training job page in an AI platform, where people watch loss, pause, cancel and deploy.
An eval or distillation run that reports a loss curve, checkpoints and a final score.
A product onboarding step that trains a custom model on the customer's data and ends in a deploy.
whenNotToUse: A generic multi-series chart with no job lifecycle: use line-chart.
A short agent task with steps rather than a loss curve: use agent-status.
Explaining how training works conceptually: use model-training.

name: trial-banner
title: Trial banner
description: A trial status banner where a ring counts down the days left, the copy names what the workspace loses, and the upgrade path is one click away. It comes as a slim banner, a sidebar card or a header pill. It shifts to a warning tone in the last days, has expired and upgraded states, and folds into the pill when dismissed or snoozed.
whenToUse: A SaaS app with a free trial that needs a quiet, always visible upgrade path.
Telling a workspace what it loses when the trial ends and nudging harder in the last days.
Showing an expired trial without blocking the app.
whenNotToUse: A hard paywall that blocks a feature; use a modal or an upgrade screen instead.
Generic announcements or release notes; use a plain banner or toast.
Usage limits (credits, seats); use a usage meter.

name: typewriter-terminal
title: Typewriter terminal
description: A terminal that types a scripted CLI session with a seeded human cadence, colors the shell syntax, and streams output lines, progress bars and spinners, with a scrubber, play/pause and replay controls.
whenToUse: A landing page hero or install section for a developer tool, SDK, or CLI.
Docs quick starts that show what each command prints before people run it.
Changelog or launch posts that show a new command in action.
whenNotToUse: Use code-block for commands and source that people need to read and copy without waiting.
Use log-stream for real, live output from a running process.
Use code-magic-move to show how a file changes between versions.

name: undo-toast
title: Undo toast
description: Archive or delete rows with a second chance: the gap closes, a countdown toast merges repeat actions, and Undo or \u2318Z puts every row back exactly where it was.
whenToUse: An inbox, notification list, task list or file list where archiving or deleting should be one click with a way back.
Bulk triage, where people remove several items quickly and one toast should summarise them all.
Anywhere a confirmation dialog would slow down a routine, reversible action.
whenNotToUse: Irreversible destruction such as deleting a project or revoking keys; use confirm-popover so the consequence is stated first.
General app notifications that are not tied to removing list items; use toast-stack.
Lists of hundreds of visible rows animating at once; virtualise the list and remove through the ref handle instead.

name: upgrade-prompt
title: Upgrade prompt
description: An upgrade nudge for the moment someone hits a limit. It shows a usage meter at 50 of 50 AI credits, a rolling price with a monthly and yearly toggle, three concrete unlocks with real model marks, and Upgrade or Maybe later. Upgrading leads into a success state with the new limits, and the card never changes size between states.
whenToUse: An AI product that hits a usage limit (credits, generations, seats) and needs a tasteful, conversion focused nudge.
A paywall moment inside an app, in a dialog, popover or inline in place of the blocked result.
Offering one next plan with a monthly and yearly price.
whenNotToUse: Comparing several plans side by side: use a pricing table or plan picker.
Buying prepaid credits without a plan change: use credit-topup.
Passive usage reporting on a billing page: use a usage meter.

name: vector-search
title: Vector search
description: Documents drop onto a tilted embedding plane and fold into points that cluster by topic; the index links neighbours, a query is typed, embedded and lowered onto the plane, a signal hops along the graph toward it, and a widening ring lights the nearest documents with connecting lines, similarity scores and a ranked list.
whenToUse: A feature section on semantic search, AI answers, or retrieval over a team's docs.
Docs pages introducing embeddings, nearest neighbour search, or approximate indexes.
whenNotToUse: Use search-index to explain keyword search with an inverted index.
Use a real scatter or cluster chart to show an actual embedding projection.

name: voice-orb
title: Voice orb
description: A voice mode orb that listens, thinks, and speaks, with a live transcript and call controls.
whenToUse: A voice mode for an assistant where the user needs to see whether it is listening, thinking, or speaking.
Hands-free or call-like flows that need start, mute, a running clock, and end in one compact control.
Live captions under a speaking agent, via VoiceTranscript.
whenNotToUse: Use voice-recorder when the user records a clip to send or save.
Use chat-thread with text-stream for typed chat where no audio is involved.
Use progress or skeleton for a generic loading state; the orb implies a voice session.

name: voice-recorder
title: Voice recorder
description: Record with a live waveform, review and scrub, then send the take into the thread.
whenToUse: Voice notes in chats, comments, or field notes where speaking beats typing.
A thread of voice bubbles with playback and scrubbing.
whenNotToUse: Use now-playing for music or long-form audio.
Use hold-to-confirm for press-and-hold actions that do not record.
Use stopwatch to time something without audio.

name: wallet-stack
title: Wallet stack
description: Fan a stack of cards and lift one out to see its activity.
whenToUse: A few payment cards, passes, or memberships where people open one to see its balance and activity.
Fintech or wallet screens that want a physical card metaphor with realistic materials.
whenNotToUse: Use card-stack for generic swipeable content that is not a card wallet.
Use a plain list or data-grid for many accounts.
Use expandable-card when one card just needs to grow in place.
